The collider phenomenology, including production mechanisms, decay patterns, and kinematic distributions, differs significantly among the various representations, providing complementary information to either confirm or exclude these interpretations of the CDF anomaly.

We present a detailed investigation of the magnetic properties of complex vanadium phosphates M(VO)₂(PO₄)₂ (M = Ca and Sr) through magnetization, specific heat, ³¹P NMR measurements, and band structure calculations. Experimental data reveal competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, producing a near-zero Curie-Weiss temperature despite a magnetic susceptibility maximum at 3 K. Specific heat and NMR measurements indicate weak exchange couplings with thermodynamic energy scale ~5 K. The reduced magnetic specific heat maximum suggests strong spin system frustration. Band structure calculations demonstrate that M(VO)₂(PO₄)₂ compounds possess essentially three-dimensional spin systems with frustration arising from competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions. Antiferromagnetic long-range ordering occurs at TN ≈ 2.1 K and 1.9 K for calcium and strontium compounds, respectively. This spin model represents an unusual example of controllable frustration in three-dimensional magnetic systems, offering insights into the interplay between crystal structure, magnetic interactions, and geometric frustration in transition metal phosphates.

# Abstract

This work provides a comprehensive overview of key galactic science questions that will be addressed by next-generation very high energy (VHE) gamma-ray instruments. These future facilities are envisioned to deliver approximately tenfold improvement in sensitivity at their central energy around 1 TeV, while critically extending observational capabilities across a broader energy range—from tens of GeV to tens of TeV. This expansion will bridge the gap between current VHE observations (limited by MAGIC's threshold) and Fermi's sensitivity at lower energies, enabling true broadband coverage. We discuss scientific opportunities across multiple galactic source populations, including pulsars and pulsar wind nebulae, binary systems, supernova remnants, stellar populations, and their associations. These enhanced capabilities will enable unprecedented studies of particle acceleration mechanisms, cosmic ray production, and the high-energy universe. The improved sensitivity and extended energy coverage will be transformative for understanding the most energetic processes in our Galaxy and resolving long-standing questions in high-energy astrophysics.

# Abstract

We investigate Bayesian inference procedures for high-dimensional linear regression models under sparsity assumptions. Our approach employs spike-and-slab priors, which combine point masses at zero with continuous distributions for non-zero coefficients. Under standard compatibility conditions on the design matrix, we establish that the posterior distribution contracts at the minimax optimal rate for estimating the unknown sparse regression vector and achieves optimal prediction risk for the response vector. Additionally, we prove that the posterior consistently identifies the true sparse support, or at least recovers coefficients significantly different from zero. We characterize the limiting shape of the posterior distribution and utilize this asymptotic theory to construct credible sets with proper frequentist coverage properties for uncertainty quantification. These results provide theoretical justification for full Bayesian methods in high-dimensional sparse regression, demonstrating their ability to adapt to unknown sparsity while maintaining optimal statistical performance.

We investigate the metal-insulator transitions at finite temperature for the Hubbard model with diagonal alloy disorder. Using dynamical mean-field theory with the non-crossing approximation combined with the coherent potential approximation, we analyze the excitation spectrum for various correlation strengths @xmath0 and disorder levels. At integer filling, two successive metal-insulator transitions occur with increasing @xmath0. Doping induces a selective transfer of spectral weight, while temperature strongly influences the low-energy dynamics. Our detailed analysis reveals the interplay between electronic correlations, disorder, and thermal effects in determining the system's transport properties and phase transitions.

# Abstract

This paper presents a comprehensive analytical framework for optimizing the design of ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes employing Davies-Cotton reflector geometry. We demonstrate that for telescopes operating in the very-high-energy gamma-ray regime, the primary design constraints—field-of-view requirements determined by physics considerations and photo-sensor dimensions limited by available technology—are sufficient to uniquely determine all other optical design parameters when light concentrators are incorporated.

A key innovation is the derivation of an analytical expression for the point-spread function (PSF) of tessellated Davies-Cotton reflectors through Taylor series expansions validated against extensive ray-tracing simulations. By including higher-order terms, we achieve percent-level precision in PSF characterization across the field-of-view. We introduce a critical design relationship linking the PSF degradation at the field-of-view edge to the angular size of camera pixels, establishing a self-consistent system of equations that naturally determines optimal values for focal length, mirror radius, and pixel dimensions.

The methodology yields comprehensive design curves spanning the typical parameter space of Cherenkov telescope systems, enabling rapid evaluation of design trade-offs. This approach facilitates direct comparison of configurations with equivalent physics performance, thereby identifying the most cost-effective solutions—a crucial consideration for large arrays.

Particular emphasis is placed on solid light concentrators, which offer approximately factor-of-two improvement in concentration ratio compared to conventional hollow designs. This enhancement enables the utilization of compact photo-sensors such as Geiger-mode avalanche photodiodes (G-APDs), potentially reducing costs while maintaining performance. We apply this framework specifically to design options for the Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA), comparing a configuration employing 60mm diameter sensors with hollow Winston cones against an alternative using 36mm diameter sensors with solid concentrators. The analysis demonstrates how modern compact photo-sensor technologies, when properly integrated with optimized concentrator optics, can achieve comparable optical performance while offering advantages in modularity, cost, and technological scalability for next-generation atmospheric Cherenkov detector arrays.

# Abstract

We investigate the low-energy quantum spectral properties of two-dimensional rectangular billiards containing small finite-size scatterers using self-adjoint extension theory. Beginning with pointlike scatterers, we establish the mathematical framework through functional analysis and identify conditions under which wave chaos emerges. The transition from pointlike to finite-size scatterers is achieved via systematic basis truncation. Our analysis reveals that wave chaos signatures in low-energy quantum states are maximally pronounced when the scatterer exhibits weak attractive potential. We demonstrate these theoretical predictions through numerical calculations of rectangular billiards with small rectangular scatterers. The results elucidate the interplay between scatterer properties, quantum spectral statistics, and chaotic behavior in confined geometries, providing insights into quantum-classical correspondence in mesoscopic systems with internal obstacles.

We investigate the phase diagram of the Anderson-Falicov-Kimball model with nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor hopping using dynamical mean-field theory. At half-filling, we analyze the system's chemical potential through geometric and arithmetic averaging methods. The model incorporates on-site energies with long-range correlated disorder, which produces system characteristics resembling those generated by random independent variable distributions. Our results demonstrate that reducing the strength of correlated disorder leads to a suppression of the extended metallic phase. This work provides insights into how different types of disorder correlations affect the metal-insulator transition in strongly correlated electron systems, highlighting the interplay between electronic correlations and spatial disorder patterns.

# Abstract

Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) and Green's Function Monte Carlo (GFMC) methods provide powerful computational approaches for studying light nuclear systems with realistic nuclear interactions. We discuss recent advances in GFMC techniques, particularly the extension to multiple states sharing identical quantum numbers. Employing the Argonne @xmath2 two-nucleon potential combined with the Illinois-2 three-nucleon interaction yields accurate predictions for binding energies across nuclei up to @xmath3C. We present several significant findings: binding energy comparisons with no-core shell model calculations demonstrate good agreement; modern nuclear Hamiltonians consistently predict an unbound tetra-neutron system; computational challenges arise when determining root-mean-square radii of extremely weakly bound systems like @xmath4He; center-of-mass corrections significantly affect extracted spectroscopic factors; and the introduction of artificial external confining potentials shows promise for studying neutron-rich isotopes. These results demonstrate the maturity and versatility of quantum Monte Carlo methods for ab initio nuclear structure calculations.

We present a comprehensive theoretical study of four-nucleon systems using the realistic coupled-channel potential CD-Bonn + @xmath0, which incorporates the excitation of a single nucleon to a @xmath0 isobar. Our investigation encompasses both the bound state and scattering processes below the three-body breakup threshold, while explicitly including Coulomb repulsion between protons. The coupled-channel framework naturally generates effective two-, three-, and four-nucleon forces through @xmath0 isobar mediation, ensuring mutual consistency with the underlying two-nucleon interaction. We find that four-nucleon force contributions to observables are significantly smaller than three-nucleon force effects. Despite the explicit treatment of @xmath0 degrees of freedom, substantial disagreements with experimental data persist, indicating that additional physical mechanisms beyond single @xmath0 excitation are necessary for quantitative description of four-nucleon systems. These results have important implications for understanding the role of many-body forces in light nuclei.

# Abstract

We investigate the structure of anisotropic strange quark stars by modeling the radial pressure as a superposition of the isotropic pressure plus a Gaussian perturbation term. Assuming a proportionality relationship between electric charge density and matter density, we numerically solve the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations for various configurations. Our analysis demonstrates that anisotropy significantly enhances both the maximum mass @xmath0 and corresponding radius @xmath1 of strange quark stars. Specifically, an anisotropy amplitude of @xmath2 with standard deviation @xmath3 yields stellar masses reaching 1.97@xmath4, consistent with observational constraints. We find that electric charge further increases the maximum mass and radius while amplifying the anisotropy factor. Notably, the tangential pressure @xmath5 and anisotropy factor @xmath6 exhibit maxima at the stellar surface, unlike the radial pressure @xmath7, with these surface maxima becoming more pronounced when electric charge effects are included. Comparative analysis reveals that anisotropy provides a more substantial contribution than electric charge in increasing the maximum mass of strange quark stars, making it a crucial factor in understanding ultra-dense stellar configurations.

# Abstract

The Google Books Corpus, comprising millions of digitized books across multiple languages, presents significant opportunities for investigating cultural, social, and linguistic evolution. However, our previous research revealed substantial contamination issues in multiple versions of the corpus, with the 2009 and 2012 unfiltered English datasets and the 2009 English Fiction dataset heavily saturated with scientific and medical literature, compromising their utility for rigorous scholarly analysis. The 2012 English Fiction dataset appeared to be the most reliable subcorpus available, and we employ it here to examine language dynamics in English from 1820 to 2000.

We critically evaluate existing methodologies for quantifying word birth and death rates, proposing instead a principled framework for analyzing word flux across various relative frequency thresholds. Our approach utilizes contributions to Jensen-Shannon divergence to identify words crossing usage thresholds between consecutive decades, thereby illuminating the primary mechanisms driving lexical change.

Our findings indicate that despite considerable variation in individual word usage patterns, the overall statistical architecture of the English language exhibits remarkable stability over the two-century period examined. Additionally, we identify evidence suggesting that the 2012 English Fiction corpus contains a substantial proportion of scholarly criticism and secondary literature about fiction rather than purely fictional works. We recommend that future revisions of the Google Books Corpus implement more stringent classification procedures to distinguish critical and analytical texts from primary fictional sources, thereby enhancing the corpus's reliability for linguistic and cultural research applications.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive study of the eclipsing binary system HV 5936 in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), combining classical light curve and radial velocity analyses with ultraviolet-through-optical spectral energy distribution modeling and high-resolution optical absorption line spectroscopy. The system consists of a B0.5 V primary and a B2 III secondary component, with current masses of 11.6 M⊙ and 4.7 M⊙, respectively.

Our analysis reveals HV 5936 to be an Algol-class interacting binary that has undergone significant mass transfer. The primary star exhibits properties consistent with a normal star of its current mass, while the secondary shows clear signatures of mass accretion: it is overluminous relative to its present mass and displays a factor-of-2 enhancement in surface helium abundance. These characteristics are consistent with "Case A" mass transfer, which occurred during the core hydrogen-burning phase of the originally more massive secondary (now primary).

We derive a distance of approximately 42.6 kpc to HV 5936, corresponding to roughly 44.3 kpc to the optical center of the LMC. This distance is several kiloparsecs closer than distances derived for other LMC eclipsing binaries in our survey, suggesting that HV 5936 is located above the main LMC disk. This interpretation is supported by the system's unusually low interstellar H I column density and low reddening (E(B-V)), both consistent with predominantly Milky Way foreground material. The system's location near the LMC supergiant shell LMC 4 may also contribute to the reduced line-of-sight absorption. This study demonstrates the power of combining multiple observational techniques to characterize binary systems and probe the three-dimensional structure of nearby galaxies.

# Abstract

In this work we consider a four-compartment Brusselator system, a reaction-diffusion model arising in chemical kinetics. The reaction terms of this system are of non-constant sign, presenting significant analytical challenges. Consequently, components of the solution are not bounded a priori, and standard functional methods to derive a priori bounds fail. We prove global existence of solutions through construction of an appropriate Lyapunov functional. Furthermore, due to the sign-changing nonlinearities, the asymptotic sign condition is also not satisfied, causing additional difficulties in establishing the existence of a global attractor. These difficulties are circumvented via the Lyapunov functional constructed along with application of the uniform Gronwall lemma. We successfully prove the existence of an @xmath0 attractor for the system, improving previous results from the literature. The Hausdorff and fractal dimensions of the attractor are shown to be finite. In particular, we derive a lower bound on the Hausdorff dimension of the global attractor. We employ numerical simulations and numerical attractor reconstruction methods via nonlinear time series analysis to validate our theoretical results. The approach provides a framework for analyzing complex reaction-diffusion systems with indefinite nonlinearities.

# Abstract

We present new measurements from proton-proton collisions at √s = 7 TeV recorded with the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The study encompasses three complementary aspects of soft QCD interactions: minimum bias distributions measured in distinct phase-space regions, underlying event activity characterized relative to the highest transverse momentum track, and angular correlations between charged particles. These measurements provide stringent tests of Monte Carlo event generators across different kinematic regimes. Detailed comparisons with various Monte Carlo model predictions reveal significant sensitivities to the modeling of multiple parton interactions, color reconnection, and hadronization mechanisms, offering crucial constraints for tuning phenomenological models.

We analyze the impact of neutral-current non-standard neutrino interactions (NC NSI) on determining neutrino mass ordering in oscillation experiments. We demonstrate the existence of an exact degeneracy that simultaneously prevents the determination of both the mass ordering and the octant of the solar mixing angle @xmath0. This degeneracy operates at the probability level and remains valid for arbitrary matter density profiles, thereby affecting all classes of neutrino experiments including solar, atmospheric, reactor, and accelerator-based measurements. The degeneracy requires order-one corrections from NSI to the neutral-current neutrino-quark interaction. Critically, this degeneracy can be experimentally tested and potentially resolved through neutrino-nucleus neutral-current scattering experiments, providing a complementary approach to address this fundamental ambiguity in neutrino physics.

# Abstract

Understanding photon trajectory through the human cornea is crucial for accurate optical modeling and clinical applications. Historically, schematic eye models employed a constant or averaged corneal refractive index, neglecting the cornea's gradient refractive index (GRIN) structure. While recent models incorporate intra-corneal GRIN properties, they rely on paraxial approximations that limit their applicability to peripheral visual field analysis and non-paraxial ray tracing. We introduce the Trajectron algorithm, which implements a closed-form solution to the ray equation for constant axial GRIN media and evaluates it over piece-wise constant GRIN distributions. This approach enables precise, non-paraxial photon tracking through the cornea. Using Trajectron, we provide the first quantitative characterization of non-paraxial intra-corneal light-bending phenomena, revealing optical effects previously unaccounted for in corneal modeling. These findings have important implications for optimizing refractive surgery algorithms and improving outcomes in vision correction procedures.

We analyze one-loop QCD corrections to hadronic matrix elements of electroweak penguin operators in kaon decays. Using chiral perturbation theory, we compute corrections to both @xmath0 and @xmath1 decay amplitudes and establish general next-to-leading order relations between them. For the @xmath3 corrections to a recent chiral determination involving @xmath4(V+A) operators, we obtain a fractional shift @xmath2. Our results provide systematic next-to-leading order constraints on electroweak penguin contributions to CP-violating kaon decays, which are important for understanding the electroweak interaction structure and for precision tests of the Standard Model. The calculations demonstrate the interplay between short-distance QCD effects and low-energy hadronic physics in weak decay processes.

# Abstract

Access control models and authorization policy languages play a crucial role in designing secure systems, yet existing proposals often impose significant implementation constraints that restrict the types of authorization requests and policy structures that can be accommodated. This paper presents a formal characterization of access control model features that minimizes such restrictions, establishing a generic framework for access control system design and analysis. We use this framework to examine two critical properties: monotonicity and completeness. Monotonicity is particularly significant for attribute-based access control (ABAC) systems, as it ensures that adding attributes cannot revoke previously granted access. Our analysis reveals that XACML, the widely-adopted XML-based language and architecture for attribute-based access control, satisfies neither monotonicity nor completeness properties. Leveraging our proposed framework, we derive XACML-style attribute-based access control models that individually satisfy monotonicity and completeness requirements. This work provides both theoretical foundations for reasoning about access control model properties and practical guidance for developing more robust attribute-based authorization systems with well-defined behavioral guarantees.

We present Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) far-ultraviolet (FUV: 1516 Å) and near-ultraviolet (NUV: 2267 Å) images of the prototypical edge-on starburst galaxies M82 and NGC 253. Our initial analysis focuses on the complex ultraviolet (UV) filamentary structures observed in the starburst-driven superwinds extending into the galaxy halos. The UV luminosities measured in these halos are significantly elevated and cannot be adequately explained by continuum and line emission from shock-heated or photoionized gas alone, except possibly in the brightest filaments of M82. This suggests that the majority of the observed UV emission originates from stellar continuum radiation produced by the starburst, which is subsequently scattered into our line of sight by dust entrained in the outflowing wind. This interpretation is consistent with previous results obtained from optical imaging polarimetry studies of M82. The UV luminosity detected in the halo represents approximately 0.3% of the total bolometric luminosity of the central starburst. Detailed morphological comparison reveals a striking spatial correlation between the UV filamentary structures in both galaxies and their corresponding Hα and X-ray emission features. This correlation strongly indicates that these outflows contain cold gas and dust, some fraction of which may be expelled into the intergalactic medium (IGM). Notably, UV emission is detected in the well-known "Hα cap" located 11 kpc north of M82. If this structure formed through interaction between the wind and a pre-existing gas cloud, the presence of UV emission implies that the cloud contains dust and is therefore not primordial, but was likely tidally stripped from M82 or M81. The efficient expulsion of dust into the IGM by starburst-driven winds could have profound implications for observations of cosmologically distant objects.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the triangular kagome lattice (TKL) realized in the recently synthesized two-dimensional magnetic materials Cu₉X₂(cpa)₆ (X = F, Cl, Br), where copper sites form a novel geometry consisting of kagome triangles ("α-trimers") with smaller triangles ("β-trimers") embedded within. We develop an exactly solvable model by treating spins on α-trimers as Ising variables while allowing XXZ character for β-trimer spins, enabling precise analytical treatment of quantum fluctuations in zero applied field through a mapping to the kagome Ising model.

Our analysis yields the complete finite-temperature phase diagram, identifying seven distinct ground state phases with their associated residual zero-temperature entropies. Notably, while the pure Ising TKL exhibits a disordered spin liquid ground state with macroscopic residual entropy *S* = 0.501*k*_B per unit cell, introducing transverse quantum couplings between neighboring β-spins dramatically reduces this to *S* = 0.108*k*_B per unit cell, demonstrating that quantum fluctuations substantially lift the classical degeneracy.

Under applied magnetic field, we map the system to a kagome Ising model with three-spin interactions, revealing rich magnetic-field-induced phenomena. Even infinitesimal fields stabilize a novel phase corresponding to a non-intersecting loop gas on the kagome lattice, characterized by entropy *S* = 0.323*k*_B per unit cell and partial magnetization of the α-spins (*m* = 1/3 per site). At moderate fields, a critical spin liquid phase emerges that maps exactly to close-packed dimers on the honeycomb lattice, remarkably persisting even when β-spins approach the Heisenberg limit. These results provide quantitative predictions for the exotic magnetic behavior of TKL materials and establish connections to fundamental models in statistical mechanics, offering insights into quantum spin liquid physics in geometrically frustrated magnets.

The intergalactic medium (IGM) temperature traces its thermal history, encoding signatures of cosmic reionization through the balance between adiabatic cooling and UV photo-heating. Reionization introduces a sudden entropy injection that increases gas temperature, broadening Lyman-α absorption features in quasar spectra. We develop a wavelet-based methodology to objectively characterize these line widths and measure IGM temperature evolution. Using high-resolution hydrodynamical simulations, we validate that our algorithm reliably detects temperature variations of ≈50% on velocity scales ∼10 km s⁻¹. Applying this technique to a high-resolution UVES/VLT spectrum of quasar Q0055-269 at z∼3, we identify a statistically significant (99% confidence) temperature increase below z∼3, consistent with the expected thermal signature of hydrogen reionization. This detection provides direct observational evidence for the reionization epoch through its imprint on the IGM thermal state, demonstrating the power of precision Lyman-α forest analysis for constraining the timing and energetics of this critical phase transition in cosmic history.

# Abstract

Ring-like ripples observed on icicle surfaces represent a morphological instability phenomenon occurring at the ice-water interface during ice growth beneath supercooled water films. These ripples characteristically exhibit wavelengths of approximately 1 cm, remarkably invariant with respect to ambient temperature, icicle radius, and water flow rate. The system involves a complex moving boundary problem featuring two distinct interfaces: the water-air surface and the advancing ice front. Previous theoretical investigations of this ripple-forming instability, notably the model by Ueno (Phys. Rev. E **68**, 021603, 2003), assumed quiescent air conditions surrounding the icicle. This study extends that theoretical framework by incorporating natural convection airflow effects at the water-air interface. We investigate whether natural convection significantly influences the characteristic wavelength of surface ripples. Our analysis evaluates the relative importance of convective heat transfer compared to the intrinsic interfacial instability mechanisms. The results provide insights into the dominant physical processes governing ripple formation and assess the validity of the static air approximation in previous models, advancing our understanding of pattern formation in ice growth phenomena.

# Abstract

We investigate the formation of large-scale structure in a cosmological model where generalized Chaplygin gas (GCG) provides the background dynamics while cold dark matter (CDM) drives structure formation. Through analytical and numerical analysis, we examine both linear and non-linear growth regimes in this unified dark matter-dark energy framework. While the model successfully reproduces standard cosmological distance measurements without invoking a cosmological constant, distinguishing it observationally from ΛCDM through geometric tests alone proves difficult. However, structure formation provides a stringent observational constraint. We demonstrate that even modest deviations of GCG parameters from the ΛCDM limit result in significant suppression of structure growth. Current large-scale structure observations therefore severely restrict the viability of GCG models, indicating that the standard ΛCDM cosmology remains strongly favored by the combined constraints from both geometric and growth-of-structure tests.

We investigate the microscopic origins of thermodynamic chaos in the Baxter-Wu model through comparison with triangular antiferromagnets and analysis of disordered system analogies. The relationship between these models reveals fundamental challenges in characterizing systems with infinitely many order parameters. We propose methods to address this complexity and extend our analysis to the Baxter-Wu model in a complex magnetic field. Our results demonstrate the existence of an infinite spectrum of critical exponents, providing insight into the unusual critical behavior and phase structure underlying thermodynamic chaos in this exactly solvable statistical mechanical system.

# Abstract

We investigate soft recollisions in strong-field ionization, where laser-driven electrons undergo distant Coulomb interactions with their parent ions. These soft collisions lead to energy bunching: electrons with varying initial drift momenta acquire momentum transfers that precisely compensate for their initial differences, resulting in convergence to discrete energy values. This bunching mechanism produces a characteristic series of peaks in the photoelectron spectrum. We demonstrate theoretically that individual peaks in this series can be systematically revealed through experiments using carrier-envelope phase-stabilized few-cycle laser pulses of progressively increasing duration, providing a controllable method to map the complete spectral structure and validate the soft recollision dynamics.

# Abstract

Conical inclusions embedded in lipid bilayer membranes, such as integral and peripheral membrane proteins, viral particles, and specialized lipid domains, locally deform the membrane and generate spontaneous curvature. We present an analytical framework combining membrane bending elasticity and translational entropy of inclusions to describe membrane budding and vesiculation phenomena. The model demonstrates that when inclusions are positioned on highly curved membrane regions with radii comparable to their characteristic length scale, membrane-mediated repulsive interactions become effectively screened. This screening facilitates inclusion aggregation at high concentrations, triggering sequential bud formation and eventual vesicle fission. While bending energy considerations alone successfully predict equilibrium bud radii, incorporating translational entropy proves essential for determining size distributions during vesicle splitting events. Specifically, energy minimization predicts asymmetric daughter vesicles, whereas entropy maximization drives equal partitioning. The theoretical predictions show excellent quantitative agreement with recent molecular dynamics simulations, providing physical insight into the competing energetic and entropic contributions governing membrane remodeling processes in biological systems.

# Abstract

We investigate the entropy of the two-dimensional @xmath0-@xmath1 model using its 12th order high temperature series expansion. Direct Padé extrapolation of the entropy series exhibits poor convergence for temperatures below @xmath2. To address this limitation, we develop an improved extrapolation method by exploiting the exact polynomial structure of the series coefficients. By subtracting a scaled version of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet entropy series from the @xmath0-@xmath1 entropy series, we achieve significantly enhanced low-temperature convergence. This technique enables us to obtain reliable results across the full range of electron densities and temperatures. The electron density enters as an adjustable parameter in the series coefficients, allowing precise determination of both the entropy's density dependence and its density derivative at fixed temperature @xmath3. We find that the density derivative exhibits strong temperature dependence, contrasting sharply with noninteracting models. Furthermore, this density derivative provides an approximation to the experimentally measurable thermopower, offering important insights for experimental studies.

We present a systematic method for reducing one-loop tensor integrals with five and six external legs to scalar master integrals. Our approach utilizes recurrence relations connecting integrals across different space-time dimensions. The reduction formulas are expressed compactly using signed minors and implemented in the Mathematica package Hexagon.m. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness through various numerical examples, providing a practical tool for multi-leg loop calculations in quantum field theory applications.

# Abstract

The phase function is a fundamental component in radiative transfer models describing light scattering by particulate surfaces. It characterizes how individual particles scatter incident light as a function of scattering angle, typically parameterized by the asymmetry parameter @xmath0 (controlling the width of the scattering lobe) and the backscattering fraction @xmath1 (determining the preferential scattering direction). Hapke's widely-adopted analytical framework provides a practical approach for modeling the spectro-photometric properties of granular planetary surfaces.

Recently, Hapke (2012, Icarus, 221, 1079-1083) compiled empirical measurements from natural samples and identified a distinctive "hockey stick" relationship between @xmath0 and @xmath1, excluding certain parameter ranges (@xmath2 and @xmath3). This correlation lacks theoretical justification, raising questions about whether it represents intrinsic material properties or systematic observational artifacts.

This study investigates potential biases introduced by parameter retrieval methodologies. We implement an advanced Bayesian inversion framework to rigorously quantify uncertainties in photometric parameter estimation. Analysis of Emission Phase Function (EPF) data reveals that parameter uncertainties themselves follow the hockey stick pattern, suggesting this relationship may arise from mathematical coupling between @xmath0 and @xmath1 within the Hapke model formulation rather than reflecting genuine physical phenomena. However, the full Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF) datasets predominantly used in Hapke's original compilation appear unaffected by this artifact.

The Bayesian approach enables systematic assessment of whether specific observational geometries provide sufficient constraints for reliably determining surface parameters, including single scattering albedo, macroscopic roughness, phase function parameters (@xmath0, @xmath1), and opposition effect characteristics. We conduct comprehensive sensitivity analyses simulating diverse surface scattering behaviors under various geometric sampling configurations: single disk-resolved images, EPF-like measurements, and BRDF-like observations.

Our results establish optimal geometric conditions for accurate photometric parameter retrieval, providing crucial guidance for designing future observational campaigns and instrumentation. These findings have significant implications for planetary remote sensing strategies, enabling more reliable characterization of surface composition and texture from spacecraft and ground-based observations. The methodology demonstrates how Bayesian uncertainty quantification can reveal subtle coupling effects between model parameters and inform observation planning.

We present a comprehensive kinematic analysis of the Galactic bulge using high-precision proper motion measurements from the Sagittarius Window Eclipsing Extrasolar Planet Search (SWEEPS) project, conducted with the Advanced Camera for Surveys/Wide Field Channel (ACS/WFC) on the Hubble Space Telescope. Proper motions are successfully extracted for more than 180,000 objects, with approximately 81,000 stars measured to better than 0.3 mas yr⁻¹ accuracy in both coordinates.

Our analysis yields several significant results: (1) Kinematic discrimination between bulge and disk populations enables extraction of a clean sample of ~15,000 bulge objects based on proper motion detections, with less than 5% disk contamination. This sample reveals the first detection of candidate blue stragglers in the bulge population. (2) Utilizing photometric distance moduli on a star-by-star basis and leveraging the large sample of high-quality proper motion measurements, we dissect the bulge's three-dimensional kinematic structure as a function of line-of-sight distance. This enables derivation of the stellar circular velocity curve from proper motions alone, which we compare with curves obtained from radial velocity measurements. (3) We trace the evolution of the velocity ellipsoid as a function of depth through the bulge, providing constraints on its dynamical structure. (4) Finally, we employ the density-weighted proper motion distribution of tracer stars to assess kinematic membership probabilities for the sixteen transiting planet candidates discovered in the Sagittarius Window field. The kinematic distribution of these candidates is consistent with membership in either the disk or bulge stellar populations, providing important constraints on their nature and origin.

We analyze the decay mode $B \to K\pi$ emphasizing its unique feature of having no factorizable contribution. Within chiral perturbation theory, treating the $B$ meson as heavy, the leading-order factorizable amplitude vanishes. We calculate nonfactorizable contributions at order $\mathcal{O}(p^3)$ from chiral loop diagrams. Additionally, employing a heavy-light chiral quark model, we evaluate nonfactorizable tree-level terms, also of order $\mathcal{O}(p^3)$, which are proportional to the gluon condensate. Our results demonstrate that both chiral loop corrections and gluon condensate contributions yield amplitudes comparable in magnitude to the experimental measurements, suggesting these nonfactorizable effects are essential for understanding this decay channel.

# Abstract

We present comprehensive results from 27 _ASCA_ observations of 26 radio-quiet quasars (RQQs) selected from the Palomar Green (PG) survey. While not constituting a statistically complete sample, these objects provide a reasonably representative cross-section of RQQs in the PG survey catalog. For the majority of sources, the _ASCA_ data are presented here for the first time, significantly expanding our understanding of X-ray emission properties in this class of active galactic nuclei (AGN).

Detection was achieved for all sources except two objects that exhibit broad absorption lines (BALs) in their optical spectra, consistent with expectations for these systems. The temporal variability characteristics observed in our sample are consistent with those found in Seyfert 1 galaxies, suggesting similar emission mechanisms operate across different luminosity ranges of radio-quiet AGN.

Time-averaged spectral analysis in the 2-10 keV (quasar rest-frame) band reveals that a simple power-law model provides an acceptable description for all but one dataset. The distribution of best-fitting photon indices spans @xmath0, with mean @xmath1 and dispersion @xmath2. This distribution closely resembles that observed in other radio-quiet AGN samples and shows no apparent correlation with X-ray luminosity, suggesting that the hard X-ray continuum generation mechanism is relatively independent of source power.

Analysis of the full 0.6-10 keV (observed-frame) continuum reveals greater spectral complexity. No single model adequately describes all sources: approximately 50% can be fit with a simple power law or exhibit only subtle deviations, while most remaining datasets display convex spectra that flatten toward higher energies. A notable exception is PG 1411+442, which shows substantial obscuration with column density @xmath4 covering approximately 98% of the continuum source.

Soft excess emission below ~2 keV is detected in only 5 (possibly 6) of 14 objects with @xmath6, a lower fraction than in some AGN samples. Furthermore, no universal spectral shape characterizes these soft components, suggesting multiple physical origins. PG 1244+026 exhibits a relatively narrow emission feature centered at @xmath8 keV (rest-frame), possibly indicating unique physical conditions in this source.

The detection rate of warm absorbers (ionized absorption) is lower than observed in Seyfert 1 galaxies, potentially reflecting selection effects inherent to the sample. However, when detected, the absorbers exhibit column densities and ionization parameters comparable to those in Seyfert 1s, suggesting similar physical structures.

Iron Kα-shell emission is evident in at least 8 RQQs, all relatively low-luminosity objects. Line parameters are consistent with other low-luminosity radio-quiet AGN. Importantly, construction of mean data/model ratios stratified by luminosity reveals systematic trends: both the profile and equivalent width of Fe Kα emission vary with source luminosity, providing important constraints on the geometry and physical conditions of the X-ray emitting regions and suggesting luminosity-dependent changes in the inner accretion disk or surrounding material.

# Abstract

We investigate the feasibility of obtaining spatially resolved spectroscopy of massive galaxies (@xmath0) at high redshift (@xmath1) using a future multi-object, adaptive optics (AO)-assisted integral field spectrograph on the European Extremely Large Telescope (E-ELT). Understanding galaxy mass assembly as a function of cosmic time represents one of the primary science drivers for this next-generation facility. Our study addresses whether such observations can effectively map the physical and chemical properties of distant galaxies selected from anticipated large-area optical to near-infrared surveys.

We generated approximately one thousand numerical simulations of three-dimensional spectroscopic observations, incorporating realistic assumptions regarding site characteristics, telescope specifications, instrumental capabilities, and the physical properties of high-redshift galaxies. These synthetic data cubes were analyzed using standard observational techniques to derive realistic kinematic measurements, allowing us to assess the sensitivity of key science objectives to both observational parameters (site, telescope, and instrument characteristics) and physical parameters (intrinsic galaxy properties).

Our analysis particularly focused on quantifying the impact of AO performance on achieving science goals. The results reveal no critical threshold effects with respect to most parameters, including telescope diameter. However, we identify telescope thermal background emission as a significant limiting factor, particularly affecting observations in the highest redshift bin (z@xmath25).

Based on our simulations, we demonstrate that a comprehensive survey of @xmath3 galaxies satisfying the full range of scientific objectives is achievable through a @xmath4 90-night observing program on the E-ELT, contingent upon the instrument providing a multiplex capability of @xmath5 or greater. These findings validate the feasibility of systematic studies of galaxy kinematics and dynamics at cosmic noon using next-generation extremely large telescopes equipped with advanced AO systems and multi-object integral field spectroscopy capabilities.

# Abstract

We investigate the temporal dynamics of power scattering from lossless chaotic cavities coupled to a single port. While the ensemble-averaged scattered power exhibits a universal power-law decay at large times, individual cavity realizations display a characteristic transition from power-law to exponential decay when excited by finite-duration pulses. We demonstrate that this transition exhibits universal behavior when time is appropriately normalized. Specifically, we define a crossover time at which fluctuations in the reflected power from individual realizations become comparable to the ensemble-averaged value. Through numerical simulations across randomly chosen cavity realizations and various pulse shapes, we show that the probability distribution function of reflected power collapses onto a universal curve when expressed as a function of time normalized to the crossover time. This universality provides fundamental insight into the statistical properties of wave chaotic systems and establishes a predictive framework for understanding power decay transitions in complex electromagnetic environments.

We investigate the collider phenomenology of bilinear R-parity violating (RPV) supergravity, which provides a minimal framework for incorporating neutrino masses consistent with oscillation data into supersymmetric models. At the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the high center-of-mass energy enables direct probes of these models through supersymmetric partner searches. We analyze how R-parity violation affects standard supersymmetry search strategies, focusing on the decay of the lightest supersymmetric particle (LSP) through bilinear RPV interactions. These decays reduce the expected missing transverse momentum signature, thereby diminishing discovery reach in conventional supersymmetry channels. However, RPV interactions significantly enhance final states with isolated same-sign dileptons and trileptons, partially compensating for losses in fully inclusive searches. We demonstrate that searches for displaced vertices arising from LSP decays substantially extend the coverage of supergravity parameter space. We present projected reaches for integrated luminosities of 10 fb⁻¹ and 100 fb⁻¹, comparing them with predictions for the R-parity conserving minimal supergravity model. Our results highlight the importance of dedicated search strategies tailored to RPV scenarios and demonstrate that displaced vertex signatures provide crucial complementary information for exploring bilinear RPV supergravity at the LHC.

# Abstract

We develop a tropical geometric framework for understanding conifold transitions in Calabi-Yau manifolds through the lens of mirror symmetry. Building on the Gross-Siebert program, which interprets mirror symmetry via Legendre duality between affine manifolds with singularities, we introduce tropical analogues of key concepts: tropical nodal singularities, tropical conifolds, and their resolutions and smoothings. 

Our main results provide a tropical interpretation of classical obstructions to deformation theory. We identify specific tropical 1-cycles through nodes in tropical conifolds that encode global obstructions to both complex smoothings and symplectic small resolutions of nodal Calabi-Yau manifolds. Remarkably, we prove that the existence of such tropical cycles guarantees the simultaneous vanishing of obstructions to smoothing a Calabi-Yau and resolving its mirror. 

We conjecture that these tropical cycles enable corresponding tropical operations: resolving the tropical conifold and smoothing its dual, thereby realizing the mirror correspondence between resolutions and smoothings at the tropical level. The conjecture is proven for special nodal configurations, and we analyze several illuminating examples demonstrating the interplay between tropical geometry and classical mirror symmetry.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive study of linear particle transport in stochastic media, a fundamental problem relevant to neutron diffusion in randomly mixed immiscible materials, light propagation through engineered optical materials, and inertial confinement fusion. Building upon the foundational work of Adams, Larsen, and Pomraning, recently revisited by Brantley, we develop benchmark configurations for mono-energetic and isotropic transport through Markov binary mixtures across multiple dimensions. Our approach utilizes Poisson random tessellations to generate stochastic media in three distinct geometries: one-dimensional slab (@xmath1), two-dimensional extruded (@xmath2), and full three-dimensional (@xmath3) configurations. For each realization, particle transport is simulated using Monte Carlo methods, enabling computation of transmission and reflection coefficient distributions on the geometry's free surfaces. We calculate ensemble-averaged values across multiple realizations to establish robust statistical measures. Notably, reference solutions for two- and three-dimensional Poisson tessellations have not been previously reported in the literature. Our results provide essential benchmark data for validating approximate yet computationally efficient models for particle transport in Markov stochastic media, including the widely-used chord length sampling algorithm, thereby advancing both theoretical understanding and practical applications in this field.

# Abstract

We investigate the effects of strong quantising magnetic fields on low-density stellar matter using the Thomas-Fermi-Dirac (TFD) model with Wigner-Seitz cell structure. Our analysis reveals significant modifications in the properties of low-density matter under intense magnetic field conditions. Notably, the magnetic field decay time scale decreases by at least two orders of magnitude compared to field-free calculations. These results have important implications for understanding the evolution of magnetized neutron stars and white dwarfs, where such extreme magnetic field configurations are believed to exist. The TFD approximation provides a self-consistent treatment of the quantum mechanical and electromagnetic effects in this regime.

# Abstract

We investigate the superconducting proximity effect in graphene-based Josephson junctions in the long diffusive regime under varying magnetic field conditions. At low temperatures, zero magnetic field, and high doping levels, high-quality interfaces and robust phase coherence enable a zero-resistance superconducting state. A remarkable suppression of the critical current emerges near graphene's charge neutrality point, which we interpret as evidence of specular Andreev reflection at charge puddle boundaries—a phenomenon unique to Dirac materials that has previously eluded experimental observation. Employing superconducting electrodes with high critical fields allows us to probe the proximity effect in the quantum Hall regime at elevated magnetic fields. While direct supercurrent detection proves challenging in our two-terminal geometry, we observe interference effects consistent with Cooper pair injection into quantum Hall edge states. These findings illuminate the interplay between superconductivity, Dirac physics, and topological quantum states in graphene.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive theoretical framework for elastic wave scattering by spherical inclusions in solid media through an extended optical theorem formulation. The optical theorem, a fundamental principle in wave scattering theory, relates the extinction cross-section to the forward scattering amplitude. Here, we generalize this theorem for elastic waves using vector spherical harmonics decomposition, applicable to various inclusion types including rigid, cavity, elastic, viscoelastic, and layered spheres. Our formulation expresses the extinction cross-section—defined as the time-averaged power removed from the incident beam normalized by its intensity—in terms of partial-wave expansion coefficients. We specifically derive the optical theorem for longitudinal spherically focused beams and employ this framework to calculate acoustic radiation forces on embedded inclusions. Numerical investigations examine iron spheres in aluminum matrices and stainless steel spheres in tissue-mimicking soft solids, computing scattering efficiencies and radiation force characteristics. Significantly, our solid-solid scattering model reveals deviations up to @xmath0 compared to conventional liquid-based approximations, highlighting the importance of shear wave coupling in elastic media. These findings have important implications for multiple applications: ultrasound elastography for tissue characterization, nondestructive evaluation of materials and structures, and the design of ultrasonically-activated medical implants. The theoretical framework provides essential tools for accurate prediction and optimization of elastic wave manipulation in solid-state systems, advancing both fundamental understanding and practical implementations in acoustoelastic applications.

We present an extended analysis of the interacting holographic Ricci dark energy (IRDE) model in non-flat cosmologies. Using recent observational data from Type Ia supernovae (SNIa), baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropy, and Hubble parameter measurements, we constrain the model parameters. Our results indicate that the fractional energy density of spatial curvature is constrained to @xmath0 @xmath1 @xmath2 @xmath1 @xmath3 when dark energy-matter interactions are included. Notably, we find that in the absence of such interactions, observational data disfavor a spatially flat universe within this theoretical framework, highlighting the crucial role of dark sector interactions in the IRDE model's viability.

# Abstract

We investigate the Hamiltonian cycle problem for linear-convex supergrid graphs, a special subclass of supergrid graphs. Supergrid graphs are finite induced subgraphs of the infinite two-dimensional supergrid structure and generalize both traditional grid graphs and triangular grid graphs. While the Hamiltonian cycle problem is known to be NP-complete for general supergrid graphs, grid graphs, and triangular grid graphs, we establish positive results for the restricted case of linear-convex supergrid graphs.

Our main contributions are twofold. First, we prove that every 2-connected linear-convex supergrid graph is locally connected, meaning that the neighborhood of each vertex induces a connected subgraph. This structural property is crucial for establishing the existence of Hamiltonian cycles. Second, building on this result, we demonstrate that every 2-connected linear-convex supergrid graph contains a Hamiltonian cycle. These findings provide an efficient solution to the Hamiltonian cycle problem for this important graph class, with practical applications in controlling stitching traces for computerized sewing machines.

Our work identifies a polynomially solvable case of an otherwise NP-complete problem and provides theoretical foundations for automated manufacturing applications. The relationship between k-connectivity, local connectivity, and Hamiltonian properties in supergrid structures offers insights into the complexity boundaries of this fundamental graph theory problem.

This paper presents QOperAv v1.5, a freely available Java application with source code for generating quantum circuits. QOperAv serves as a code generator that produces quantum circuits capable of evaluating averages of the form $\langle f(A)\rangle$ with polynomial efficiency, where $f$ is a polynomially computable function and $A$ is a Hermitian operator, assuming polynomial compilation of $e^{iAt}$ is feasible. The software implements algorithms from previous research, integrating standard quantum computing techniques including quantum phase estimation and quantum multiplexors. This tool facilitates practical implementation of quantum expectation value calculations for computational applications.

# Abstract

Carbon-rich grains condense in core-collapse supernova ejecta within a year of explosion, with silicon carbide (SiC) grains of type X found in primitive meteorites carrying isotopic signatures of explosive nucleosynthesis. A rarer subgroup, type C grains, exhibits anomalous isotopic patterns: isotopically heavy silicon and light sulfur, contradicting standard models. We propose that C grains originate from carbon-rich stellar material experiencing lower shock temperatures than type X grains during supernova passage. In this framework, the extreme @xmath0Si enrichments in C grains result from the presence of short-lived @xmath0Si (@xmath1@xmath2 = 153 years) produced via neutron capture on stable silicon isotopes in the ejecta. This mechanism naturally explains the observed @xmath0S enrichments without requiring mixing of deeper silicon-rich layers or silicon-sulfur fractionation through molecular chemistry. The @xmath0Si abundance in these grains provides valuable constraints on neutron densities achieved in carbon-rich helium shell material during the explosion. We discuss the significant impact of uncertainties in neutron capture cross sections for isotopes in the @xmath0Si mass region on these interpretations. Our model offers a self-consistent explanation for the distinctive isotopic signatures of C grains while providing new diagnostics for understanding neutron-capture processes in supernovae. These results have important implications for constraining supernova nucleosynthesis conditions and interpreting presolar grain data.

# Abstract

Understanding cybersecurity posture through data-driven approaches remains a critical yet under-explored challenge in network security research. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of real-world data collected by CAIDA's network telescope during March 2013 to formalize and characterize cybersecurity posture. We introduce a novel framework that examines three fundamental time series perspectives: the number of victims (telescope IP addresses under attack), the number of observed attackers, and the total number of detected attacks. Our methodology focuses on identifying statistical properties and phenomena within these time series to extract meaningful cybersecurity insights.

Key contributions include the introduction of the "sweep-time" concept, demonstrating that it must be modeled as a stochastic process rather than a simple random variable. Our analysis reveals significant concentration effects, where attackers and attacks originating from specific countries dominate the overall attack landscape observed by the telescope. Furthermore, we provide empirical evidence regarding the importance of telescope scale, showing that substantially smaller network telescopes may offer limited utility compared to larger-scale monitoring infrastructure. These findings have important implications for designing effective network monitoring systems and understanding global cyber threat patterns. Our work establishes a foundation for systematic, data-driven characterization of cybersecurity posture using network telescope observations.

# Abstract

We investigate the neural response characteristics of Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) neuron ensembles to transient spike train inputs using wavelet transformation (WT) analysis. The study examines ensembles of varying sizes (@xmath0 = 1, 10, 100, and 500 neurons) receiving transient @xmath1-pulse spike trains (@xmath2) embedded in independent Gaussian noise. Signal transmission fidelity is quantified through cross-correlation metrics expressed via WT expansion coefficients, while signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is evaluated using wavelet-based denoising methods to isolate noise contributions from output signals.

Our results demonstrate that while single neurons (@xmath3) exhibit unreliable responses to sub-threshold transient signals in noisy conditions, transmission fidelity—assessed through cross-correlation and SNR—improves substantially with increasing ensemble size @xmath0. This enhancement reveals the critical role of neural populations in mediating stochastic resonance (SR) for transient spike inputs. Additionally, we show that in large-scale ensembles, weak noise intensities that facilitate SR for sub-threshold inputs produce minimal degradation in transmission fidelity for supra-threshold transient spikes. These findings elucidate the population-level mechanisms underlying reliable signal transmission in noisy neural systems and demonstrate the utility of wavelet-based analysis for characterizing transient neural signals.

# Abstract

Interfacing disparate quantum technologies requires flexible control over single-photon properties, particularly spectral and temporal characteristics. We present a comprehensive framework for quantum optical waveform manipulation based on sum-frequency generation combined with classical pulse shaping techniques. Using non-perturbative theoretical analysis, we identify parameter regimes enabling simultaneous high-efficiency and high-fidelity conversion of single-photon Gaussian waveforms while preserving quantum coherence. Our investigation reveals that when phase-matching conditions are sufficiently broadband relative to input spectral widths, time-ordering effects introduce negligible aberrations, enabling near-ideal waveform conversion. We analyze the preservation of energy-time entanglement throughout the conversion process, demonstrating that quantum correlations remain intact under appropriate conditions. These results establish that sum-frequency generation with pulse shaping provides a viable route toward implementing quantum time lenses and arbitrary waveform conversion with unit fidelity. Such capabilities are essential for quantum networking applications requiring efficient interconnection of heterogeneous quantum systems operating at different wavelengths and employing distinct temporal modes for information encoding and transmission.

# Abstract

We prove that magnetic flows on compact oriented surfaces cannot be magnetically isospectral to geodesic flows with negative curvature when both systems satisfy hyperbolicity conditions. Specifically, we show that a magnetic flow associated with a Riemannian metric and non-zero magnetic field cannot have the same length spectrum of topologically corresponding periodic orbits as a negatively curved geodesic flow with equal total volume. The proof employs regularization techniques inspired by Hamenstädt's methods for handling the singularities arising in the comparison of these dynamical systems. This result establishes a fundamental rigidity property distinguishing magnetic flows from purely geodesic flows in the hyperbolic setting, demonstrating that the presence of a magnetic field introduces spectral characteristics that cannot be replicated by metric deformation alone.

# Abstract

We report on the evolution over the last ~9 Gyr of cosmic history (since z ≈ 1.3) of late-type galaxy populations in the Chandra Deep Field-North (CDF-N) and Extended Chandra Deep Field-South (E-CDF-S) survey fields. Our late-type galaxy sample consists of 2,568 galaxies identified using rest-frame optical colors and morphologies. We utilized X-ray stacking analyses to investigate the X-ray emission from these galaxies, emphasizing the contributions from normal star-forming galaxies not dominated by active galactic nuclei (AGNs).

Over this redshift range, we find significant increases (factors of 5-10) in the mean X-ray-to-optical luminosity ratio (L_X/L_B) and the mean X-ray-to-stellar mass ratio (L_X/M_*) for galaxy populations selected by optical luminosity and stellar mass, respectively. When analyzing galaxy samples selected via star formation rate (SFR), we find that the mean ratio (L_X/SFR) is consistent with being constant over the entire redshift range for star-forming galaxies, thus demonstrating that X-ray emission can be used as a robust indicator of star-formation activity out to z ≈ 1.3.

We find that the specific star-formation activity (as traced by X-ray luminosity) per unit stellar mass in a given redshift bin increases with decreasing stellar mass over the redshift range 0 < z < 1.3, consistent with previous studies of how star-formation activity depends on stellar mass. Finally, we extend our analyses to Lyman break galaxies at z ≈ 3 and estimate that L_X/L_B at z ≈ 3 is similar to its value at z ≈ 1.3, suggesting continued evolution of X-ray emission properties in star-forming galaxies to higher redshifts.

# Abstract

We demonstrate control over quantum dynamics in chaotic kicked rotor systems through strategic modification of the kicking field. Our approach enables manipulation of several quantum coherent phenomena, including enhancement of dynamical localization length and introduction of classical anomalous diffusion-assisted control in regimes far from semiclassical limits. We observe diverse strongly nonexponential lineshapes characterizing dynamical localization. These results exemplify controlled quantum dynamics in classically chaotic systems, revealing that subtle field modifications can dramatically alter quantum behavior. Our findings open new avenues for exploring quantum fluctuations and correlations in quantum chaos, demonstrating that quantum coherence effects can be systematically tuned even when underlying classical dynamics remain chaotic, with implications for quantum simulation and control protocols.

We address the inverse problem of designing isotropic pairwise particle interaction potentials that lead to the formation of a desired lattice structure when a system of particles is cooled, motivated by the goal of producing materials with pre-specified properties. We present two approaches: a heuristic computation-free geometric method and a fast, robust trend optimization method, both successfully generating high-quality honeycomb lattices. The trend optimization method proves particularly effective due to its ability to efficiently handle the noisy and computationally expensive objective functions characteristic of self-assembly design problems. Additionally, we demonstrate anisotropic potentials that robustly produce kagome lattices, a structure not previously achieved using isotropic potentials. These methods provide promising strategies for rational design of interaction potentials to achieve target crystalline structures in self-assembling systems.

# Abstract

We investigate the cosmological evolution of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) using total gamma-ray fluence as a measure of burst strength. This analysis requires understanding both the distributions of spectral parameters and total fluence distribution of GRBs, which are significantly affected by detector selection effects. We present novel non-parametric statistical techniques to properly account for these selection biases and apply these methods to estimate the intrinsic distribution of the spectral peak energy (@xmath1) in the @xmath0 spectrum from the observed distribution. Our distributions are derived from four-channel data and should be considered preliminary estimates; accordingly, we emphasize methodological development and present qualitative results. Using the derived spectral parameters, we calculate total fluence for individual bursts and compute cumulative and differential distributions. These distributions enable us to estimate the cosmological rate evolution of GRBs across three different cosmological models. Our principal findings are twofold: (1) Based on our spectral parameter estimates, a substantial population of high-@xmath1 bursts may exist below the BATSE detection threshold, potentially biasing our understanding of the GRB population; (2) The inferred GRB co-moving rate density exhibits markedly different behavior compared to other extragalactic populations, particularly diverging from recently determined cosmic star formation rates. These results have important implications for understanding GRB progenitors and their relationship to stellar evolution.

# Abstract

We investigate water absorption in the metal-organic framework Cu-BTC using density functional theory calculations at the meta-GGA+U level, examining concentrations up to 3.5 H₂O molecules per Cu ion. Our calculations reveal that absorbed water molecules arrange into chains connected by hydrogen bonds, with a pronounced tendency to form closed cage structures at higher concentrations. The stability of these water clusters arises from multiple synergistic interactions: water-water hydrogen bonding, Cu-water oxygen coordination, van der Waals forces, electric field enhancement of intermolecular interactions, and hydrogen bonding between water and framework oxygen atoms. These stable cluster configurations provide a molecular-level explanation for the exceptionally strong water affinity observed in Cu-BTC and similar metal-organic frameworks featuring coordinatively unsaturated metal sites. Our findings suggest that the formation of these robust water assemblies is a key factor governing water uptake behavior in this important class of porous materials, with implications for applications in gas storage, separation, and catalysis where water stability is a critical consideration.

# Abstract

We present an experimental test of Hardy's quantum paradox using a novel single-photon approach that exploits two compatible degrees of freedom within the same particle: spin angular momentum (polarization) and orbital angular momentum (optical transverse mode). Unlike traditional implementations requiring photon pairs, our single-particle configuration simplifies experimental complexity and enhances detection efficiency. While this approach sacrifices the ability to invoke locality arguments for enforcing non-contextuality—requiring instead explicit assumptions based solely on observable compatibility—it offers significant practical advantages. The simplified architecture and improved detection efficiency present a promising pathway toward addressing detection loopholes that plague conventional two-particle experiments. Our results demonstrate that Hardy's paradox can be effectively tested through intra-particle correlations, opening new avenues for fundamental quantum mechanics tests while mitigating technical challenges associated with multi-particle entanglement and detection limitations.

# Abstract

We investigate a class of surfaces in Riemannian 3-spaces characterized as graphs with prescribed projections of principal direction fields onto a base surface @xmath0. The central problem involves determining such surfaces when both principal curvatures are specified along a curve in @xmath0. This geometric problem is reformulated as a Cauchy problem for systems of quasilinear partial differential equations. Under appropriate regularity conditions on the initial data, we establish that these equations are hyperbolic and admit unique local solutions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that parallel curved (PC) surfaces in space forms constitute a distinguished class of global solutions satisfying weaker regularity requirements. For this special class, explicit construction via iterative function sequences is possible. The results provide new insights into the interplay between geometric constraints and analytic properties of surface equations in Riemannian geometry.

**Keywords:** Riemannian space, surface, principal curvature/direction, hyperbolic PDEs

**AMS Subject Classification:** 53B20, 53B25, 53C99, 53A05

# Abstract

We investigate the thermodynamical properties of a photon gas within a phase space characterized by compact spatial momentum space, motivated by doubly special relativity theories and noncommutative spacetime structures. Our analysis reveals that at the high temperature limit, both the internal energy and entropy possess finite upper bounds determined by the compactness scale of the momentum space. The maximum internal energy is constrained to the order of Planck energy, while the entropy bound is fixed by the dimensionless factor @xmath0, established through identification of the momentum space size with the Planck scale. Remarkably, this entropy bound exhibits striking similarity to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of black holes. This correspondence suggests a profound connection: black hole thermodynamics may emerge naturally from saturated thermodynamic states within a comprehensive quantum gravitational statistical mechanics framework. Our results indicate that quantum gravity effects, encoded in the noncommutative phase space structure, fundamentally limit thermodynamical quantities and may provide microscopic foundations for black hole entropy, bridging quantum gravity phenomenology with statistical mechanics.

We investigate the collider phenomenology of a heavy fourth generation top quark (@xmath0) in a two Higgs doublet model extended with a fourth generation of fermions (4G2HDM), demonstrating that search strategies optimized for the minimal fourth generation standard model (SM4) may not be adequate. While SM4 assumes the dominance of the @xmath1 decay mode, we show that alternative decay channels can be significant in extended models. Specifically, we examine the recent CMS lower bounds of @xmath2 GeV (semi-leptonic channel @xmath3) and @xmath4 GeV (dilepton channel @xmath5), which were derived using SM4-motivated search strategies. Our analysis reveals that when the decay @xmath6 dominates, the standard CMS search tools yield a substantially weaker lower bound of only @xmath7 GeV. This significant relaxation of the mass limit highlights the model-dependent nature of heavy quark searches and indicates that current experimental constraints may not apply universally to all fourth generation scenarios. We propose an alternative search strategy specifically designed to probe physics beyond the naive SM4 framework and improve sensitivity to the potentially richer dynamics of fourth generation fermions in extended models.

We report systematic studies of Zn substitution effects in the electron-doped cuprate Ca@xmath1Na@xmath2CuO@xmath3Cl@xmath3 near the critical hole concentration of 1/8 per Cu. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a substantial suppression of superconducting transition temperature (@xmath0) and reduced superconducting volume fraction upon minimal Zn doping (0.51%). Most notably, these effects are maximized at hole doping @xmath4≈0.14, coinciding with the emergence of anomalous behavior. Complementary muon spin relaxation (@xmath12SR) experiments demonstrate significant slowing of Cu spin fluctuations below 5 K in this doping regime. The observed phenomena closely parallel behavior in archetypal cuprates YBa@xmath3Cu@xmath5O@xmath6 and Bi@xmath3Sr@xmath3Ca@xmath7Y@xmath2Cu@xmath3O@xmath8, establishing that Zn-induced stripe correlations represent a universal characteristic of high-@xmath0 superconductors, extending beyond the La@xmath9CuO@xmath10 family to encompass diverse cuprate structures.

# Abstract

We present novel lower bounds for randomized multiparty communication complexity using a new proof technique called *symmetrization*. This technique offers a natural, intuitive, and more accessible alternative to existing methods such as the information cost approach for establishing communication complexity bounds.

Our results span two fundamental communication models: the blackboard model, where messages are broadcast to all players simultaneously, and the message-passing model, where communication occurs through player-to-player channels. For the canonical problem of computing the coordinate-wise XOR of bit-vectors, where each of $n$ players holds a length-$m$ vector, we establish tight lower bounds of $\Omega(nm)$ in the blackboard model. For analogous problems involving OR and AND operations, we prove lower bounds of approximately $\Omega(nm)$ in the message-passing model (when $n = O(1)$) and $\Omega(nm)$ in the blackboard model.

Beyond these foundational results, we demonstrate the versatility of symmetrization by deriving lower bounds for several other fundamental problems, including bit-wise majority computation, graph connectivity, and various other tasks, suggesting broad applicability of the technique. Importantly, all our lower bounds hold even for randomized protocols with two-sided error, making them robust against probabilistic computation.

Our communication complexity lower bounds have direct implications for the functional monitoring model (also known as the distributed streaming model), yielding new space-time tradeoffs for distributed computation over data streams. Additionally, we leverage the symmetrization technique to establish several direct-sum-type theorems for multiparty communication, further demonstrating its power and flexibility as a proof tool for understanding the fundamental limits of distributed computation.

# Abstract

We present deep radio continuum observations of globular clusters (GCs) in M81, a nearby spiral galaxy, to search for intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) through their accretion signatures. Using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array at 5.5 cm wavelength with 1.5″ (26.4 pc) resolution, we observed 206 probable GCs previously identified with the Hubble Space Telescope. No individual GC is detected in our observations, including 49 massive clusters with stellar masses exceeding @xmath1. We performed weighted-mean stacking analysis on both the full sample and the massive cluster subsample, yielding non-detections in both cases.

We employ two independent methods to constrain IMBH masses. First, using a semi-empirical accretion model assuming the hard X-ray state, our 3σ radio luminosity upper limits correspond to IMBH mass limits of @xmath3 for the all-cluster stack and @xmath4 for the massive-cluster stack. Second, we apply the fundamental plane relation to two X-ray-detected clusters, deriving 95% confidence upper limits of @xmath5 and @xmath6 for their individual IMBH masses.

Our results provide stringent constraints on IMBH occupation fractions in M81 GCs and demonstrate that no analog of HLX-1—an ultraluminous X-ray source and strong IMBH candidate in an extragalactic star cluster—exists among the M81 GC population. This highlights the exceptional or rare nature of the HLX-1 system. The absence of detectable IMBHs in this well-studied GC system has implications for IMBH formation channels, the seeding of supermassive black holes in the early universe, and predictions for gravitational wave detection by future space-based missions. These observations underscore the challenges in detecting quiescent or low-accretion-rate IMBHs in extragalactic GCs and suggest that either IMBH occupation fractions are low or that most IMBHs in GCs are accreting at extremely sub-Eddington rates.
