We investigate the existence and stability of bright solitons in self-defocusing (SDF) media with spatially modulated quintic nonlinearity, extending recent findings for cubic nonlinearities. In such systems, bright solitons can be stabilized without external linear potentials when the nonlinearity coefficient increases sufficiently rapidly from center to periphery. We examine both one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) configurations, with potential implementations in nonlinear optics, particularly colloidal suspensions of nanoparticles, and in the description of Tonks-Girardeau gases of ultracold bosons for the 1D case.

For the 1D system with nonlinearity modulation function @xmath0, we obtain a family of exact analytical solutions for fundamental solitons and construct generic solutions numerically. We develop both Thomas-Fermi approximation (TFA) and variational approximation (VA) methods, introducing a novel "raised @xmath1" variational ansatz that significantly outperforms the conventional Gaussian ansatz in accuracy. 

The stability analysis of fundamental (nodeless) 1D solitons is performed through eigenvalue calculations for small perturbations and confirmed via direct numerical simulations, demonstrating complete stability. Higher-order solitons with two nodes exhibit a limited stability region, while modes with more than two nodes are entirely unstable. Our results confirm that the recently proposed "anti-Vakhitov-Kolokolov" (anti-VK) stability criterion for fundamental bright solitons in SDF systems remains valid for quintic nonlinearities. Additionally, we present particular exact solutions for 2D solitons, demonstrating the genericity of the stabilization mechanism across different dimensionalities and nonlinearity types. These findings establish that spatially modulated SDF media provide a robust platform for supporting stable bright soliton states across various nonlinear regimes.

# Abstract

We develop holographic techniques for computing spectral functions and analyzing quasi-particle excitations in strongly coupled non-equilibrium systems. Our approach provides a gravity dual perspective on key aspects of Landau Fermi-liquid theory, including space-time dependent shifts in quasi-particle energy and spin during non-equilibrium evolution. 

A central finding is that the standard incoming wave boundary condition at the event horizon is insufficient for constructing a well-defined perturbative expansion of non-equilibrium observables. We resolve this issue by carefully analyzing regularity requirements at the horizon, establishing a universal prescription that enables systematic perturbative calculations for any thermalizing non-equilibrium state, independent of microscopic details.

Our formalism reveals that non-equilibrium spectral functions encode information about the system's relaxation modes. Furthermore, we argue that in generic non-supersymmetric theories with holographic duals, there exists a window in the temperature-chemical potential plane at large @xmath0 where non-equilibrium states far from hydrodynamic equilibrium can be effectively characterized by a finite set of low-dimension operators. This suggests a form of universal non-equilibrium behavior in strongly coupled systems.

These results establish a framework for studying far-from-equilibrium quantum matter using holographic methods, with potential applications to heavy-ion collisions, quantum quenches, and strongly correlated condensed matter systems.

# Abstract

Cosmic rays at the highest energies represent one of the most intriguing puzzles in modern astrophysics, with individual particles carrying macroscopic energies approaching that of a well-thrown baseball. The origin and propagation mechanisms of these ultra-high energy cosmic rays remain poorly understood, prompting diverse theoretical explanations from conventional astrophysical acceleration processes to exotic physics beyond the Standard Model and primordial universe phenomena. High-energy neutrinos provide a crucial complementary probe, as they are inevitably produced in cosmic ray interactions and propagate undeflected by magnetic fields, potentially revealing their sources directly. Recent experimental advances in detection techniques, combined with multi-messenger observations incorporating gamma-ray astronomy, promise significant statistical improvements at the highest energies. The imminent detection of ultra-high energy neutrinos through novel experimental approaches will open unprecedented opportunities to constrain source models and test fundamental physics at energy scales far beyond terrestrial accelerators. This review examines the rapidly developing interplay between cosmic ray and neutrino astrophysics, emphasizing emerging experimental methodologies and their potential to probe physics beyond the electroweak scale.

# Abstract

We investigate the critical behavior and nonequilibrium aging dynamics of the gauge-glass and XY spin-glass models in three dimensions using a novel numerical approach. The nonequilibrium aging method (NAM) employed here determines critical temperatures and nonequilibrium scaling exponents through systematic analysis of two-time correlation and integrated response functions for both spin and chiral degrees of freedom. We first validate NAM by studying the ferromagnetic XY model, demonstrating excellent agreement with established equilibrium and nonequilibrium results. 

Applying NAM to the gauge-glass model yields significantly improved precision in determining critical quantities compared to previous estimates. For the XY spin-glass model, we perform comprehensive simulations with both Gaussian and bimodal bond distributions, calculating spin and chiral two-time correlation and integrated response functions. Our results provide compelling evidence for a spin-chiral decoupling scenario, particularly pronounced in systems with Gaussian interactions and observable in bimodal cases. This decoupling manifests as chiral degrees of freedom exhibiting finite-temperature ordering, while spin degrees of freedom order only at very low or zero temperature. 

The NAM framework proves to be a powerful and reliable tool for characterizing phase transitions in frustrated magnetic systems with quenched disorder, offering advantages over conventional equilibrium methods in accessing critical properties and revealing the distinct ordering behaviors of spin and chiral sectors in glassy systems.

# Abstract

We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of a bouncing ball moving vertically in a gravitational field while colliding with a periodically moving limiter. The limiter's displacement is described by a cubic function of time, enabling analytical computations. We derive the Poincaré map that describes the evolution from one impact to the next. Various dynamical modes are analyzed both analytically and numerically, including fixed points, @xmath0-cycles, and chaotic bands. Our analysis reveals that chaotic bands emerge from fixed points following the first period-doubling bifurcation through a corner-type bifurcation mechanism. We obtain an exact solution for the timing of consecutive impacts when two impacts occur within the same period of the limiter's motion, facilitating a rigorous analysis of chattering phenomena. The cubic limiter function's simplicity allows for detailed analytical treatment while capturing essential features of the system's complex dynamics.

# Abstract

We present comprehensive X-ray and multiwavelength observations of eight high-luminosity active galactic nuclei (AGNs) at @xmath1 exhibiting distinctive disc-like H@xmath0 emission-line profiles, selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data Release 7. These sources represent a relatively unexplored population at higher redshifts and luminosities compared to previously studied disc-like emitters, filling an important gap in the luminosity-redshift parameter space.

X-ray spectroscopic analysis reveals that seven sources display typical AGN characteristics with power-law photon indices of @xmath2≈2.0. Among these, two exhibit moderate X-ray absorption with column densities @xmath3@xmath4 @xmath5 consistent with neutral gas. The remaining source, J@xmath6, shows extreme X-ray weakness with only three detected hard photons, indicating heavy obscuration (@xmath7 @xmath5). Notably, this object is identified as a low-ionization broad absorption line (BAL) quasar based on Mg@xmath8II @xmath9 absorption features, representing the first reported case of a disc-like emitter that is also a BAL quasar.

The infrared-to-ultraviolet spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of all eight sources closely resemble those of typical luminous quasars, including a prominent UV "bump" characteristic of efficient accretion from geometrically thin, optically thick discs. This contrasts markedly with lower-luminosity disc-like emitters. Analysis of the optical-to-X-ray power-law slope parameters (@xmath10) reveals no significant X-ray excess emission in these high-luminosity systems.

Energy budget considerations indicate that efficient illumination and ionization of the outer disc by the inner disc is required across all disc-like emitters, with approximately @xmath11 of the nuclear ionizing radiation needed on average. This illumination likely occurs through direct irradiation and/or scattering processes. For high-luminosity objects, warped accretion disc geometries appear necessary to facilitate direct illumination, as their geometrically thin inner discs in flat configurations would insufficient solid angle coverage for effective outer disc irradiation. These results provide important constraints on accretion disc physics and geometry in luminous AGNs.

# Abstract

This paper addresses stabilization of nonlinear continuous-time systems using finite-valued controls or measurements. A discontinuous variant of the semi-global backstepping lemma serves as the fundamental analytical tool. We establish robust practical stabilizability through quantized and ternary control strategies, demonstrating their effectiveness via hysteresis-based switching mechanisms. The theoretical framework accommodates measurement quantization and control signal discretization while maintaining system stability properties. Applications to representative nonlinear control problems illustrate the practical utility of the proposed approach, showing that finite-valued feedback can achieve satisfactory performance despite information constraints inherent in quantized implementations.

We investigate the nucleosynthesis signatures of two distinct classes of massive core-collapse supernovae and their connection to extremely metal-poor (EMP) stars. Recent observations have identified: 1) hypernovae with kinetic energies exceeding @xmath0 erg, approximately 10 times that of normal supernovae, and 2) faint supernovae with energies @xmath1 0.5 @xmath2 @xmath3 erg. Both classes are candidates for black-hole-forming supernovae, potentially with rotating or non-rotating black holes. We compare theoretical nucleosynthesis yields from these events with observed abundance patterns in EMP stars to constrain the nature of Population III (first generation) supernovae. Our analysis demonstrates that EMP stars, particularly those exhibiting carbon enhancement, show abundance patterns consistent with enrichment by black-hole-forming supernovae. These results provide crucial insights into the properties of the first stellar explosions and early chemical evolution of the Galaxy.

# Abstract

We investigate the short-distance behavior of heavy quark potentials in SU(3) and SU(4) gauge theories using the thick center vortex model. By enhancing vortex flux contributions near trivial center elements that pierce Wilson loops and incorporating fluctuations in vortex core sizes, we successfully reproduce a Coulombic potential consistent with Casimir scaling at short distances. The model simultaneously captures all essential features of the confining potential: an intermediate-range linear component obeying Casimir scaling and a large-distance regime determined by the N-ality of the representation. These results demonstrate that the thick center vortex framework provides a comprehensive phenomenological description of the heavy quark potential across all distance regimes, from perturbative to confining scales, validating its utility for understanding the full dynamics of color confinement.

# Abstract

This paper investigates the asymptotic properties of massless scalar fields propagating in non-commutative Schwarzschild black hole backgrounds near spatial infinity. In these modified geometries, non-commutativity manifests through a mass function that depends on both the radial coordinate @xmath0 and a non-commutativity parameter @xmath1. We analyze solutions to the zero-rest-mass scalar wave equation by reducing the problem to solving an inhomogeneous Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation, wherein the parameter @xmath1 explicitly influences the source term structure.

Our analysis reveals that for finite non-commutativity parameters, the qualitative behavior mirrors that found in standard general relativity: the conformal singularity at spacelike infinity significantly restricts the differentiability class of scalar fields at future null infinity. Consequently, in the physical space-time, scalar fields exhibit slower asymptotic decay rates compared to their flat space-time counterparts. This degraded fall-off behavior represents a characteristic feature shared between non-commutative and commutative black hole geometries, suggesting that certain asymptotic properties are robust against non-commutative modifications. These findings contribute to understanding how quantum gravity-inspired non-commutativity affects wave propagation in curved space-times while preserving essential features of classical general relativistic dynamics at infinity.

# Abstract

An asymptotically exact continuum dislocation theory for single crystal bars under torsion is developed. We demonstrate that the dislocation distribution minimizing the bar's energy at zero torque is uniform. For non-zero applied torque, the energy-minimizing configuration exhibits a dislocation-free zone in the outer ring of the bar's cross-section. The equilibrium dislocation distribution and twist angle per unit length are determined analytically as functions of the applied torque. When energy dissipation is incorporated, an elastic core region emerges, with dislocations concentrated in an intermediate ring bounded by two dislocation-free zones. This configuration fundamentally alters the stress distribution, thereby increasing the critical torque threshold. The analysis combines variational calculus and asymptotic methods to provide explicit relationships between applied torque, dislocation patterns, and mechanical response, offering new insights into plasticity in torsional loading of crystalline materials.

# Abstract

We present comprehensive simulations of a novel automated metrology system for the alignment and mechanical stability monitoring of future linear colliders. The Linear Collider Alignment and Survey (LICAS) instrument combines laser straightness monitors (LSM) for straightness measurements with frequency scanning interferometry (FSI) for absolute distance determination. Our detailed simulations model a LICAS system integrated within a Rapid Tunnel Reference Surveyor (RTRS) train configuration. Results demonstrate the feasibility of achieving vertical alignment accuracy on the order of micrometers over kilometer-scale tunnel sections, meeting the stringent specifications required for the TESLA linear collider design. This automated approach offers significant advantages for continuous monitoring and correction of mechanical deformations in extended linear accelerator structures.

# abstract

low-ionization metal absorption systems, particularly the mg ii λλ2796,2803 doublet, serve as important tracers of cold gas around galaxies at cosmological distances. however, the physical origin of this gas remains debated: whether it represents material in large proto-galactic disks, dwarf galaxy halos, or cold gas entrained in supernova-driven galactic outflows. statistical studies employing stacking analyses and clustering measurements have suggested that strong mg ii absorbers preferentially trace dense, cold gas in starburst-driven winds. this scenario predicts that the strongest absorption systems should be associated with vigorous star formation activity.

we present results from a near-infrared integral field spectroscopic survey using sinfoni to directly test this prediction by searching for hα emission around strong mg ii absorbers at z ~ 1. for our sample of 21 absorbers with rest-frame equivalent widths w_r ≥ 1 å, we detect hα emission in 67% (14/21) of cases. these detections lie within ±200 km s⁻¹ of the wavelength predicted from the absorption redshift and at impact parameters ranging from 0.2 to 6.7 kpc from the background quasar sightline. the inferred star formation rates from hα luminosities range from 3-100 m_⊙ yr⁻¹, exceeding the m82 starburst by factors of 2-50 on average.

our 3σ flux sensitivity of ~10⁻¹⁷ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻², corresponding to sfr ~ 0.5 m_⊙ yr⁻¹, represents a significant improvement over previous ground-based absorption-selected galaxy surveys. we find tentative evidence (2σ significance) for a positive correlation between star formation rate and mg ii equivalent width, supporting a physical connection between starburst activity and strong absorption signatures. dynamical modeling of resolved velocity fields in several systems indicates host halo masses of ~10¹² m_⊙, consistent with independent clustering analyses of mg ii absorbers.

# Abstract

This paper proposes a modification to Newtonian gravitation where gravitational interaction depends on surface-to-surface rather than center-to-center particle separation. This modification produces forces with nuclear-strength magnitudes between nucleons. The theoretical justification involves postulating quantum wormholes within particles that mediate gravitational interactions through graviton flux emission proportional to particle dimensions. This framework allows point-particle treatment while accounting for finite size effects. When wormhole mouths approach Planck-length separation, the resulting gravitational force between nucleons becomes enhanced by a factor of @xmath1 relative to conventional Newtonian gravity. This dramatic amplification potentially unifies gravitational and nuclear interactions at short distances, suggesting gravity's fundamental role in strong force phenomena through quantum geometric effects at the Planck scale.

We analyze electromagnetic corrections to the dominant octet weak nonleptonic decay amplitudes using chiral perturbation theory. The calculation includes contributions from photon exchange and the electromagnetic mass difference between charged and neutral mesons. We find that these corrections induce relative shifts in amplitudes at the few percent level, which may be relevant for precision tests of the Standard Model in weak decays. The formalism is developed systematically within the framework of chiral perturbation theory, allowing for a model-independent assessment of electromagnetic effects in these processes.

# Abstract

Grazing Incidence Fast Atom Diffraction (GIFAD or FAD) has emerged as a powerful surface-sensitive technique for characterizing crystal surfaces. While less susceptible to thermal decoherence compared to thermal energy helium atom scattering (TEAS/HAS), GIFAD demands exceptionally high surface quality with extended coherence lengths between defects. Such pristine surfaces are achievable through fresh crystal cleavage or molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) preparation, enabling in situ GIFAD measurements. This paper provides a comprehensive methodological framework for quantitative analysis of diffraction spot intensities, building upon recent work by Atkinson et al. and Debiossac et al. We detail the experimental procedures and image processing techniques, explicitly addressing the underlying physical assumptions governing elastic fast atom diffraction. Particular emphasis is placed on differential filtering methods and systematic approaches to extract reliable intensity data from diffraction patterns, with applications to GaAs surfaces demonstrating the technique's analytical capabilities.

# Abstract

We study the spaces of polynomials stratified into sets with a fixed number of roots inside certain semialgebraic regions, on their borders, and in the complement of their closures. Our approach generalizes, unifies, and develops several classical methodologies in control theory stability problems: root clustering (ℓ-stability) developed by Kalman, Barmish, and Gutman; ℓ-decomposition by Neimark, Polyak, and Gryazina; and the universal parameter space method by Fam, Meditch, and Ackermann. The foundation of our approach lies in interpreting the correspondence between roots and coefficients of polynomials as a symmetric product morphism. We characterize the topology of strata up to homotopy equivalence and, in many important cases, up to homeomorphism. Additionally, we describe adjacencies between strata and provide an explanation for the special significance of classical stability problems, including Hurwitz stability, Schur stability, and hyperbolicity, within this unified framework.

# Abstract

We investigate vibration modes of the Skyrme model using the rational map ansatz. Our analysis demonstrates that vibrations of radial profiles and rational maps decouple, allowing separate treatment. We explicitly examine cases with $\mathbb{B}=1$, $\mathbb{B}=2$, and $\mathbb{B}=3$. Comparing our analytical results with numerical calculations by Barnes et al., we find that the rational map ansatz qualitatively reproduces the numerically obtained vibration mode structures. However, quantitative agreement is limited, with significant discrepancies observed in the predicted vibration frequencies. These findings suggest that while the rational map provides useful insight into Skyrmion dynamics, refinements may be necessary for accurate frequency predictions.

# Abstract

We present a numerical method to compute path integrals in effective SU(2) Yang-Mills theories by approximating the functional integral through summation over gauge field configurations constructed from localized building blocks. This approach successfully reproduces fundamental features of Yang-Mills theory, notably confinement. Our analysis demonstrates that confining gauge field configurations possess two essential characteristics: non-trivial topological charge and extended spatial structures. The building block decomposition provides computational efficiency while capturing the relevant physics of the vacuum structure. Results indicate that both the topological properties and the long-range correlations of field configurations play crucial roles in the confinement mechanism, offering insights into the non-perturbative dynamics of Yang-Mills gauge theories.

# Abstract

This paper addresses the computational challenge of transforming Gröbner basis orderings from degree reverse lexicographic (DRL) to lexicographic (LEX) for zero-dimensional polynomial ideals of degree @xmath1. This transformation represents a critical bottleneck in polynomial system solving, making efficient algorithmic approaches essential for practical computations.

We present several novel methods that exploit the inherent sparsity of multiplication matrices in the classical FGLM (Faugère-Gianni-Lazard-Mora) algorithm. Our main contribution is a comprehensive deterministic top-level algorithm that automatically selects the most efficient method based on input characteristics. This adaptive approach enables handling of ideals with degrees exceeding @xmath2, significantly extending the practical range of computable systems compared to existing implementations in MAGMA and Singular.

For ideals in shape position, we develop two Wiedemann algorithm-based approaches: (1) a probabilistic method achieving complexity @xmath3, where @xmath4 denotes the number of nonzero entries in a multiplication matrix, and (2) a deterministic variant computing the LEX Gröbner basis via the Chinese Remainder Theorem. For general zero-dimensional ideals, we introduce a method utilizing the Berlekamp-Massey-Sakata (BMS) algorithm from coding theory to efficiently handle multi-dimensional linearly recurring relations arising in the conversion process.

A significant theoretical contribution is our explicit formula estimating the sparsity of the principal multiplication matrix for generic polynomial systems. We prove that constructing this sparse representation incurs negligible computational cost and demonstrate that the asymptotic complexity for generic systems reduces to @xmath6, representing a substantial improvement over classical approaches.

Comprehensive complexity analyses accompany all proposed methods, providing theoretical foundations for their efficiency. Extensive experimental results validate our implementation's superior performance, demonstrating its capability to solve previously intractable problems. The combination of adaptive method selection, exploitation of structural sparsity, and specialized algorithms for different ideal configurations makes this approach particularly effective for large-scale polynomial system solving applications in computational algebra, cryptography, and related fields.

# Abstract

We demonstrate that a four-particle system confined in a one-dimensional box with two-body harmonic interactions can be described using the symmetry point group @xmath0. Group theoretical methods facilitate analysis of both small-box and large-box regimes. First-order perturbation corrections are derived for the lowest-lying states. A Rayleigh-Ritz variational calculation is performed using symmetry-adapted basis sets consistent with the system's symmetries. For the three lowest energy levels, we present alternative variational results that exhibit improved convergence for larger box dimensions. This approach illustrates the utility of group theory in treating confined quantum many-body systems with inter-particle interactions, providing accurate approximations across different confinement regimes through symmetry considerations and variational methods.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive spectral analysis of **ASCA** observations of 12 early-type galaxies, representing the largest systematic study of its kind with this observatory. The X-ray spectra are uniformly characterized by a two-component model: (1) a hard component described either by thermal emission at ~10 keV or a power-law with photon index Γ~1.8, attributed to discrete sources and/or hot gas, and (2) a soft component arising from diffuse thermal plasma with temperatures between 0.3–1.0 keV. 

The hard X-ray luminosity exhibits a tight correlation with optical blue-band luminosity, suggesting a connection to the stellar population. In contrast, the soft component luminosity shows substantial scatter with no clear correlation, indicating diverse interstellar medium properties. Metal abundances derived from soft X-ray emission are systematically sub-solar, averaging ~0.3 Z⊙, consistent with gas loss or metal-poor accretion.

Analysis of scaling relations reveals that early-type galaxies occupy a distinct parameter space compared to galaxy clusters. The volume emission measure versus temperature relation falls significantly below the extrapolation from cluster data, demonstrating that these galaxies are relatively gas-poor systems. The ratio of stellar kinetic energy density to gas thermal energy density (β) is typically less than unity, suggesting the hot gas is not in full hydrostatic equilibrium with the gravitational potential.

Importantly, we find no systematic dependence of X-ray properties on galaxy environment (field versus group/cluster membership), implying weak interaction between interstellar and intracluster media. These results provide important constraints on gas retention, heating mechanisms, and the evolutionary histories of early-type galaxies, highlighting fundamental differences in the thermodynamic states of hot gas in galaxies versus clusters.

# Abstract

Two theorems concerning gravitational time delay are proven for spacetimes satisfying the null energy condition and null generic condition. The first theorem establishes that in null geodesically complete spacetimes, for any compact set K, there exists a compact set K' such that any "fastest null geodesic" connecting points outside K' cannot enter K. This result demonstrates that in globally hyperbolic spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces, observers at sufficiently late times cannot possess particle horizons. The second theorem addresses spacetimes admitting a timelike conformal boundary, showing that if the extended spacetime satisfies strong causality and a compactness condition, then any fastest null geodesic connecting boundary points must remain entirely within the boundary. An important consequence is that generic perturbations of anti-de Sitter spacetime necessarily produce time delays relative to the unperturbed anti-de Sitter geometry. These theorems provide rigorous mathematical constraints on causal structure and demonstrate how matter satisfying energy conditions generically causes null geodesics to deviate from extremal paths, with significant implications for cosmological horizons and the stability properties of asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetimes.

# Abstract

MXNet is a multi-language machine learning library designed to streamline the development of ML algorithms, particularly deep neural networks. By embedding both declarative symbolic expressions and imperative tensor computations within host languages, MXNet provides a flexible programming interface with automatic differentiation capabilities. The system achieves high computational and memory efficiency through careful optimization and runs across diverse heterogeneous platforms, from mobile devices to distributed GPU clusters. This paper presents MXNet's API design principles and system implementation details, focusing on the unified approach for handling symbolic expressions and tensor operations. We demonstrate the framework's scalability and performance through preliminary experiments on large-scale deep neural network applications deployed across multiple GPU machines, showing promising results for practical machine learning workloads.

# Abstract

By simulating jet-inflated bubbles in cooling flows with the PLUTO hydrodynamic code, we demonstrate that mixing of high-entropy shocked jet material with the intra-cluster medium (ICM) constitutes the primary heating mechanism perpendicular to the jet axis. Heating by the forward shock proves insignificant in comparison. The mixing process exhibits remarkable efficiency in heating the ICM omnidirectionally, extending to distances of @xmath0 and beyond. Although the jets remain active for only @xmath1, the mixing and heating processes near both the equatorial plane and along the symmetry axis continue to counteract radiative cooling for extended periods of @xmath2 after jet cessation.

We discuss several implications of these findings: (@xmath3) The vigorous mixing is expected to entangle magnetic field lines, thereby suppressing global heat conduction in the central ICM regions. (@xmath4) This intense mixing generates a multi-phase ICM in the inner cluster regions, where the coolest gas parcels preferentially cool, flow inward, and fuel the active galactic nucleus, triggering subsequent jet-activity episodes. This mechanism provides additional support for the cold feedback paradigm. (@xmath5) In environments where the medium beyond the @xmath6 region exhibits lower density than typical galaxy groups and clusters—such as during galaxy formation—the forward shock and elevated pressure from shocked jet material may expel gas from the system entirely. These results highlight the complex interplay between AGN feedback, ICM thermodynamics, and cluster evolution across cosmic time.

# Abstract

We investigate symmetric partially metric association schemes with multiplicity three, where a partially metric scheme contains a connected relation whose distance-two relation remains within the scheme. Our classification reveals several notable cases: association schemes arising from regular complete multipartite graphs, schemes related to the five Platonic solids, the bipartite double of the dodecahedron, and three schemes connected to well-known arc-transitive cubic graphs—the Möbius-Kantor graph, the Nauru graph, and the Foster graph F048A. These results emerge from our comprehensive determination of symmetric association schemes having multiplicity three with a connected relation of valency three. Additionally, we construct an infinite family of cubic arc-transitive 2-walk-regular graphs possessing an eigenvalue of multiplicity three. Remarkably, these graphs generate non-commutative association schemes characterized by a symmetric relation of valency three and an eigenvalue with multiplicity three, demonstrating the rich interplay between combinatorial structures, graph theory, and algebraic properties in association schemes.

# Abstract

We introduce a proportional growth model that explains the distribution of business firm growth rates across multiple scales of economic aggregation. The model predicts an exponential distribution in the central region and power-law tails with exponent ζ ≈ 3. While previous studies have focused primarily on the Laplace-like body of growth rate distributions due to data constraints, we test our model systematically across different hierarchical levels—from individual products through firms to entire countries. Our empirical analysis confirms the model's predictions for both the complete functional form of growth rate distributions and the relationship between size and variance. These results demonstrate that proportional growth mechanisms operate consistently across diverse scales of economic organization, providing a unified framework for understanding growth rate statistics in economics.

# Abstract

We use lattice Boltzmann simulations to study the effect of shear on phase ordering of a two-dimensional binary fluid. The shear is imposed by generalizing the lattice Boltzmann algorithm to include Lees-Edwards boundary conditions. We demonstrate how the interplay between the ordering effects of spinodal decomposition and the disordering tendencies of shear leads to a dynamic steady state where domains are continually broken up and reformed. This non-equilibrium state depends critically on the shear rate and fluid viscosity. The domain morphology and characteristic length scales in the steady state are characterized, revealing how external flow fields can control phase separation dynamics in binary fluids.

# Abstract

We present spectroscopic observations of ultra-compact dwarf (UCD) candidates in the fossil group NGC 1132 using the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS). Our observations confirm six bona fide UCDs at a distance of approximately 100 Mpc with recessional velocity around 3600 km/s. The most luminous UCD exhibits properties intermediate between typical bright UCDs and compact elliptical galaxies, with an effective radius of 77.1 pc and absolute magnitude M_V = -14.8 mag, making it an M32 analog. The confirmed UCDs show a mean radial velocity of 3600 km/s and velocity dispersion of 240 km/s, comparable to poor galaxy groups. These kinematic properties demonstrate that UCDs can serve as effective dynamical tracers for studying the gravitational potential of galaxy groups. This study provides the first spectroscopic confirmation of UCDs in a fossil group environment, establishing that these objects can form under diverse evolutionary pathways and across different host systems, from rich galaxy clusters to evolved, isolated groups dominated by a single massive elliptical galaxy.

# Abstract

We investigate manifold estimation from random samples through clustering-based reconstruction methods. Specifically, we analyze piecewise constant estimators via k-means and piecewise linear estimators via k-flats clustering algorithms. Our contributions extend existing k-means theory in two key directions: (1) novel reconstruction guarantees for k-means on manifolds, and (2) pioneering reconstruction bounds for k-flats, representing the first theoretical results for higher-order manifold approximation methods. While our k-means analysis employs established mathematical frameworks applied in new contexts, the k-flats analysis requires developing entirely new theoretical tools. These results provide rigorous performance guarantees for practical manifold learning algorithms, establishing theoretical foundations for both zero-order (piecewise constant) and first-order (piecewise linear) approximation schemes in geometric data analysis.

Abstract:

For the design and optimization of CO₂ recovery from alcoholic fermentation processes by distillation, accurate models for vapor-liquid equilibria (VLE) are essential. This study presents two thermodynamic models for the ternary mixture N₂+O₂+CO₂ at low temperatures. The first approach employs the Peng-Robinson equation of state (EOS) with pure substance parameters from literature and binary parameters of the van der Waals one-fluid mixing rule fitted to experimental binary VLE data. The Peng-Robinson EOS demonstrates good agreement with both binary and ternary experimental data, showing limitations only at high pressures near the critical region.

The second approach develops a molecular-based model validated through molecular simulation using binary and ternary experimental VLE data. Henry's law constants for N₂ and O₂ in CO₂ are predicted via molecular simulation based on this validated molecular model. These predicted constants form the basis of a practical thermodynamic model specifically designed to reliably describe VLE behavior in the CO₂-rich region.

Both models provide complementary tools for process engineering applications: the Peng-Robinson EOS offers broad applicability across moderate pressure ranges, while the Henry's law-based model provides a simplified, user-friendly alternative particularly suitable for CO₂-rich conditions typical of fermentation off-gas streams. The molecular simulation approach bridges fundamental intermolecular interactions with macroscopic thermodynamic properties, offering predictive capability without extensive experimental data. These models support the development of energy-efficient CO₂ recovery processes from fermentation, addressing both environmental concerns and potential CO₂ utilization opportunities in the beverage and biofuel industries.

# Abstract

We present the MUFASA suite of cosmological hydrodynamic simulations that implement state-of-the-art physical models for galaxy formation and evolution. Utilizing the GIZMO meshless finite mass (MFM) code, MUFASA incorporates H₂-based star formation, nine-element chemical evolution tracking, two-phase kinetic outflows calibrated from the Feedback in Realistic Environments (FIRE) zoom simulations, and an evolving halo mass-based quenching prescription. Our fiducial 50 h⁻¹ Mpc volume contains 250 million resolution elements evolved to z=0. The predicted galaxy stellar mass functions (GSMFs) reproduce observations from z=0 to z=3 within cosmic variance limits, representing an unprecedented match to this fundamental diagnostic. The cosmic star formation history and stellar mass assembly show good agreement with observational constraints, exhibiting strong archaeological downsizing whereby dwarf galaxies form most of their stellar mass after z≈1. We examine resolution effects by running 25 h⁻¹ Mpc and 12.5 h⁻¹ Mpc volumes to z=2 with identical feedback implementations, with the highest resolution run resolving all hydrogen-cooling halos. These simulations demonstrate reasonable convergence in key metrics. Specific star formation rates agree well with data at z=0 but are underpredicted at z≈2 by approximately a factor of three, highlighting a persistent challenge in contemporary galaxy evolution models. We additionally compare results using MFM versus two variants of smoothed particle hydrodynamics, demonstrating that while the GSMF exhibits ~0.2 dex sensitivity to hydrodynamic methodology, this remains subdominant to uncertainties in feedback parameterization, emphasizing the primacy of physical modeling choices.

We present a comprehensive evaluation of the charged Higgs boson decay to tau lepton and neutrino within the general two-Higgs doublet model framework. Our analysis employs a nonlinear R_ξ-gauge that significantly streamlines calculations, yielding simplified expressions for both fermionic and bosonic contributions. We systematically examine the branching ratio across various parameter space regions, finding that while values as high as O(10^-4) are theoretically achievable, such parameter regions face severe constraints from recent precision measurements. These include restrictions from B→X_sγ, the muon anomalous magnetic moment, B_s mixing, and the ρ parameter, combined with exclusion limits from direct searches at CERN's LEP collider. Our results indicate substantial tension between parameter regions favoring enhanced decay rates and current experimental bounds, limiting detection prospects at future colliders.

# Academic Article Abstract

We examine the central surface brightness distribution of galaxies using the catalog of O'Neil, Bothun, & Schombert (1999), focusing on the range 22.0 ≤ μ_B(0) ≤ 25.0 mag arcsec⁻². By applying a bi-variate volume correction that accounts for each galaxy's known central surface brightness, scale length, and redshift, we extend the surface brightness distribution function by one magnitude to 25.0 B mag arcsec⁻². Our analysis reveals a flat surface brightness distribution function (slope = 0) extending from the Freeman value of 21.65 ± 0.30 to the survey limit of 25.0 mag arcsec⁻², spanning more than 11σ. This result suggests that a substantial fraction of the universe's baryonic content likely resides in gravitational potentials that are only faintly illuminated by their embedded galaxies, with significant implications for understanding the distribution of visible matter in the cosmos.

# Abstract

We present evidence for a rare class of rapidly evolving supernovae characterized by extremely fast light curves and unusually low ejecta masses. Our analysis focuses on three historical events: SN 2002bj, SN 1885A, and SN 1939B. SN 2002bj, previously identified as a peculiar Type Ib supernova, exhibited a peak absolute magnitude of M ≈ −18 mag, an extraordinarily rapid rise time of ~10 days, and a subsequent decline of 0.25 mag per day in B-band. Remarkably, the ejected mass was estimated at only ~0.3 M⊙, significantly lower than typical supernovae.

We demonstrate that two additional historical supernovae share these distinctive characteristics. Through analysis of the SN 1885A remnant in M31 and newly presented spectroscopic observations of SN 1939B, we confirm similarly rapid evolution and low ejecta masses. The environmental context of both events—SN 1885A occurring in the M31 bulge and SN 1939B in a passive elliptical galaxy—strongly indicates old white dwarf progenitor systems, consistent with thermonuclear explosion scenarios.

Notably, the spectrum of SN 1939B shows no clear helium features, contrasting with helium-shell detonation models proposed for SN 2002bj. The preferential discovery of these fast-evolving supernovae in nearby galaxies suggests a volumetric rate of approximately 1–2% of all supernovae, indicating this may represent a previously underrecognized class of stellar explosions with implications for understanding white dwarf binary evolution and explosion mechanisms.

we present new high - contrast imaging observations of the low - mass companion orbiting the nearby star hd 984, obtained as part of the gemini planet imager exoplanet survey (gpies). the observations, conducted with the gemini planet imager, include photometry in the j (1.12–1.35 μm) and h (1.50–1.80 μm) bands. by combining these new measurements with archival data from 2012 and 2014, we determine the first orbital solution for hd 984 b. our analysis yields a semi - major axis of 18 au (corresponding to an orbital period of approximately 70 years), with a 68% confidence interval ranging from 14 to 28 au. the orbital eccentricity is constrained to 0.18 (68% confidence interval: 0.05–0.47), and the inclination is 119° (68% confidence interval: 114°–125°).

to address significant spectral covariance present in the companion's spectrum, we develop a novel technique that decomposes the spectrum into low and high spatial frequency components, enabling proper treatment of correlated spectral noise. applying this method, we compare the companion's spectrum to template spectra of field brown dwarfs and low - mass stars. our best - fit classification indicates a field - gravity m@xmath0 spectral type, corresponding to an effective temperature of @xmath1 k. photometric analysis yields a bolometric luminosity of @xmath2/@xmath3 dex using dusty atmospheric models. from these models, we derive an age - dependent mass estimate ranging from @xmath4 to @xmath5 m@xmath6. these results are consistent with previous characterizations of the companion and demonstrate the efficacy of our spectral decomposition technique for analyzing high - contrast imaging data.

# Abstract

We introduce the concept of parabolic-like mappings, analogous to polynomial-like mappings but characterized by a parabolic external class with a parabolic fixed point in the external map. After establishing the definition, we investigate the dynamical properties of these mappings and prove a straightening theorem. This theorem demonstrates that any parabolic-like mapping of degree @xmath0 is hybrid conjugate to a member of the family @xmath1 \,| \, p_a(z)=z+ \frac{1}{z}+ a,\,\,a \in \c\right\}. Furthermore, when the filled Julia set is connected, this conjugacy corresponds to a unique member of the family. This result extends classical straightening theorems to the parabolic setting, providing a normal form for understanding parabolic dynamics.

We present a database implementation for storing and querying XML metadata conforming to the International Virtual Observatory Alliance (IVOA) Characterisation Data Model. Utilizing PostgreSQL's native XML type support, we developed a prototype query service offering two complementary access methods. The first employs an HTTP GET/POST interface that directly translates query parameters into XPath expressions targeting specific data model elements within the XML serialization. The second provides a web-service interface accepting XQuery statements, similarly converted to XPath for efficient metadata tree navigation. This dual-interface architecture enables comprehensive searches across characterisation metadata while maintaining compatibility with both programmatic and human-interactive access patterns. The system has been deployed in the ASPID-SR archive, serving science-ready observational data from the Russian 6-meter telescope, demonstrating practical application in large-scale astronomical data management.

# Abstract

We present a datacube covering the central 10 arcsec of the archetypal active galaxy NGC 1068 over the wavelength range 4200-5400 Å, obtained during the commissioning of the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS) installed on the Gemini-North telescope. The datacube reveals complex emission line morphology in the [OIII] doublet and Hβ line. To characterize this structure phenomenologically, we construct an atlas of velocity components derived from multiple Gaussian component fits to the emission lines. The atlas contains numerous features that cannot be readily associated with distinct physical structures. While some components are likely associated with the expected biconical outflow, others suggest high-velocity flows or disk-like structures. As a first step toward interpretation, we identify the stellar disk using kinematical maps derived from the Mg I triplet absorption feature at 5170 Å and establish associations between this and gaseous components in the atlas of emission line components. This study demonstrates the power of IFU spectroscopy for dissecting the complex kinematics of active galactic nuclei.

# Abstract

We introduce the study of pseudoknots as equivalence classes of pseudodiagrams under generalized Reidemeister moves. Pseudodiagrams are knot diagrams where crossing information may be missing at some crossings, creating ambiguity about which strand passes over. To classify these objects, we develop the weighted resolution set (were-set), a novel invariant that captures the possible classical knots arising from resolving the ambiguous crossings in all possible ways, weighted by their frequency of occurrence. We establish foundational properties of were-sets and compute them explicitly for several infinite families of pseudoknots. Additionally, we extend classical knot invariants including crossing number, bridge number, and unknotting number to the pseudoknot setting. We investigate pseudoknot analogues of fundamental concepts such as homotopy, chirality, and amphicheirality, demonstrating how classical knot theory generalizes to this framework. Our results provide the groundwork for a systematic classification theory of pseudoknots and suggest connections to quantum knot invariants and knot detection problems.

# Abstract

We develop an analytic effective medium theory to investigate mean access times for random walks on hybrid disordered structures. These structures consist of complex networks embedded into regular lattices, where transition rates @xmath0 for steps along lattice bonds differ from rates @xmath1 for steps across network shortcuts. Our theoretical framework accommodates arbitrary shortcut distributions and is explicitly applied to partially-disordered traversal enhanced networks featuring randomly distributed shortcuts of fixed length with finite probability. Numerical simulations demonstrate excellent agreement with effective medium theory predictions across all examined characteristics. We compare access times on these partially disordered structures with those on small-world networks. Our analysis reveals that small-world networks provide, on average, the most efficient mechanism for uniformly reducing access times throughout the network, outperforming other hybrid architectures in minimizing mean first-passage times for random walkers.

# Photometric Investigation of the Globular Cluster Population of NGC 1399: Color Bimodality, Radial Distribution, and Dark Matter Implications

## Abstract

We present a comprehensive photometric study of the globular cluster (GC) system surrounding NGC 1399, the dominant galaxy in the Fornax cluster, utilizing Washington C and Kron R filters across an unprecedented field of @xmath0, encompassing approximately 200×200 kpc at the Fornax distance. This investigation represents the most extensive CCD photometric survey of this galaxy's cluster system to date.

Our analysis reveals that NGC 1399's GC system extends beyond 100 kpc from the galactic center, with a color distribution exhibiting pronounced bimodality characteristic of massive early-type galaxies. The spatial distributions of the red and blue GC subpopulations show distinct radial dependencies: within ~55 kpc, red clusters display stronger central concentration compared to blue clusters. Beyond this radius, both subpopulations exhibit indistinguishable surface density profiles that closely match the galaxy's light distribution.

The surface brightness profile of NGC 1399 is remarkably well-fitted by a power law with an exponent of -1.85 and a core radius of @xmath2 across the entire radial range studied. Significantly, we detect no steepening of the luminosity profile at large galactocentric distances—a finding with important implications for understanding the galaxy's mass distribution. We propose that this extended power-law profile reflects NGC 1399's embedding within an extensive dark matter halo, which prevents the characteristic outward steepening of the stellar density profile observed in isolated galaxies.

The total GC population is estimated at @xmath3 clusters, yielding a specific frequency of @xmath4 in the V band. We observe a pronounced color gradient in NGC 1399, contrasting with the comparison galaxy NGC 1404, which shows no such gradient. Beyond this radius, both populations converge to similarly elevated local specific frequencies of ~8 and ~13 for blue and red clusters, respectively, suggesting different formation histories and assembly mechanisms for the inner and outer regions of this massive galaxy's GC system.

# Abstract

We present a detailed analysis of chemical abundance patterns in simulated stellar halos using state-of-the-art cosmological N-body + smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations. Our simulations incorporate a physically motivated supernova feedback prescription, alongside comprehensive treatments of metal enrichment, metal-dependent cooling, and metal diffusion processes. Building upon previous work, we examine galaxies whose stellar halos exhibit a dual population structure: stars accreted from disrupted satellite galaxies and stars formed in situ within the central galaxy that were subsequently displaced into the halo through merger-driven heating mechanisms.

We analyze the chemical abundance patterns, specifically [Fe/H] and [O/Fe] ratios, of halo stars within 10 kpc of solar-like observer positions in our simulated galaxies. Our key finding is that for systems without recent major mergers, in situ halo stars occupying the metal-rich tail of the metallicity distribution function display systematically elevated [O/Fe] ratios compared to accreted stars at equivalent [Fe/H] values. This bimodality in the [O/Fe]-[Fe/H] plane emerges naturally from the distinct gravitational potential wells characterizing the formation environments of these two populations: in situ stars form in the deeper potential of the main galaxy progenitor, while accreted stars originate in lower-mass satellite systems with different star formation and chemical enrichment timescales.

This predicted dichotomy shows qualitative agreement with recent observational studies of the local Milky Way stellar halo. Our results suggest that detailed measurements of multidimensional chemical abundance patterns in resolved stellar populations can serve as powerful archaeological tools, enabling observers to disentangle the relative contributions of in situ formation versus accretion processes in the assembly histories of the Milky Way and other nearby L* galaxies.

# Abstract

This paper develops combinatorial interpretations for q-analogues of Fibonacci-Stirling numbers through an extended rook theory model. Building upon previous work that introduced Fibonacci-Stirling numbers as connection coefficients between Fibonacci falling and rising factorial bases, we construct two distinct q-generalizations of these polynomial bases.

The classical Fibonacci-Stirling numbers connect the fibo-falling factorial basis @xmath4 and fibo-rising factorial basis @xmath5, which generalize standard factorial bases by incorporating Fibonacci numbers @xmath0 in their recursive definitions. These numbers admit combinatorial interpretations via rook placements on specially structured boards.

The first type uses products of q-brackets with Fibonacci number arguments: @xmath11_{\downarrow_{q, f, k}}$ ] and @xmath11_{\uparrow_{q, f, k}}$ ]. The second type uses differences of q-brackets: @xmath13}_{\downarrow_{q, f, k}}$ ] and @xmath13}_{\uparrow_{q, f, k}}$ ]. Each q-analogue generates corresponding q-Fibonacci-Stirling numbers as connection coefficients.

Our main contribution is a modified rook theory framework that provides combinatorial models for both types of q-Fibonacci-Stirling numbers. This extends the classical rook theory approach by incorporating q-weights on board configurations, yielding explicit combinatorial formulas and bijective proofs. The construction unifies the treatment of both q-generalizations while preserving the elegant structure of the original Fibonacci-Stirling theory. These results demonstrate how rook theory naturally extends to quantum analogues of generalized factorial bases.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive analysis of the vertical distribution of resolved stellar populations in six low-mass, edge-on spiral galaxies observed with the Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys (HST/ACS). Our observations reveal the presence of significant extraplanar stellar components extending up to approximately 15 scale heights (~3.5 kpc) above the galactic midplane in all sample galaxies. 

Through detailed color-magnitude diagram analysis, we investigate the vertical structure as a function of stellar age. The young stellar population (≲100 Myr) exhibits scale heights larger than comparable populations in the Milky Way, suggesting that star formation in these low-mass systems occurs in intrinsically thicker disks. A systematic age-dependent trend emerges across all galaxies: young main sequence stars, intermediate-age asymptotic giant branch stars, and old red giant branch (RGB) stars display progressively increasing scale heights. This systematic progression provides strong evidence that disk heating mechanisms contribute to the formation of extraplanar stellar structures.

By constraining disk heating rates from the observed age-height relationship, we find that heating proceeds at rates dramatically lower than those measured in the Milky Way. Analysis of RGB color distributions at high galactic latitudes indicates that the extended stellar components are moderately metal-poor, with peak metallicities around [Fe/H] ~ -1.0 and remarkably flat vertical metallicity gradients. The absence of significant metallicity gradients suggests that the majority of extraplanar RGB stars formed during early epochs rather than representing recently heated populations.

Our results demonstrate that low-mass disk galaxies possess multiple distinct stellar components similar to the Milky Way, but with different formation and evolutionary histories. We interpret our findings within the framework of both disk heating and merger scenarios, concluding that the observed vertical stellar distributions likely result from a combination of both mechanisms operating throughout the galaxies' formation histories. These observations provide important constraints on disk galaxy formation models and highlight the diverse pathways through which galactic thick disks can be assembled.

# Abstract

We systematically evaluate two important mesoscopic effects in quantum dots using realistic modeling. "Scrambling" refers to single-particle spectral changes induced by added electrons, while "gate effect" describes modifications from gate-induced shape deformation. These phenomena are analyzed using both self-consistent Kohn-Sham (KS) theory and a Fermi liquid-like Strutinsky approach. Our results demonstrate that genuine scrambling effects remain small due to the smooth potential characteristic of quantum dots. However, KS theory implicitly incorporates residual interactions within the spectrum, which dominate the response and amplify apparent scrambling. The gate effect exhibits comparable magnitude in both theoretical frameworks and, despite being relatively small, proves sufficient to induce gate-controlled spin transitions. These findings clarify the relative importance of electron-electron interactions versus geometric effects in determining quantum dot electronic structure.

# Abstract

We study non-interacting systems with power-law quasiparticle dispersion @xmath0 and random short-range-correlated potential disorder. We demonstrate that in dimensions @xmath1, unlike in lower dimensions, a critical disorder strength (set by the bandwidth) exists at which the system undergoes a disorder-driven quantum phase transition at the band bottom. This transition belongs to a universality class distinct from the conventional Anderson transition. Contrary to conventional wisdom, the transition manifests in disorder-averaged quantities such as the density of states. For symmetry classes permitting localization, a striking signature is the non-analytic behavior of the mobility edge: it remains pinned to the band bottom for subcritical disorder but grows when disorder exceeds the critical strength. We employ renormalization group techniques controlled by an @xmath2 expansion to calculate critical exponents and scaling functions characterizing the density of states at this novel transition. Our analysis applies to Dirac materials, including Weyl semimetals, where this transition occurs in the physically relevant case of three dimensions. This work reveals a new class of disorder-driven quantum criticality with observable consequences in realistic materials.

# Abstract

We examine the origin of dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the most abundant galaxy type in clusters, by evaluating two competing formation scenarios: primordial formation within the cluster environment versus transformation of infalling galaxies. Analysis of observational data from the Virgo and Perseus clusters suggests that tidal and environmental processes acting on accreted systems play a dominant role in producing these objects. Despite their seemingly delicate structure, dwarf spheroidals demonstrate remarkable resilience to disruption. The preponderance of evidence favors infall and subsequent transformation as the primary formation mechanism for cluster dwarf spheroidals, rather than in-situ formation during cluster assembly. This has important implications for understanding galaxy evolution in dense environments.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive formalism for deriving dark matter halo properties beyond two virial radii using the spherical collapse model without shell crossing, providing the theoretical foundation for predictions presented in Prada et al. (2005). Our framework enables computation of the probability distribution for the spherically-averaged enclosed density at arbitrary radii @xmath0.

# Abstract

Two competing theoretical scenarios have been proposed to explain the apparent s-wave characteristics observed in electron-doped cuprate superconductors: anisotropic s-wave pairing and d-wave pairing coexisting with antiferromagnetism (AF). We investigate the electronic structure near nonmagnetic impurities within the coexistence scenario to distinguish between these frameworks. Our calculations demonstrate that despite antiferromagnetic order creating a complete gap in the quasiparticle excitation spectrum, mid-gap resonant peaks in the local density of states (LDOS) persist around impurity sites when d-wave pairing is present. These impurity-induced states exhibit distinctive characteristics fundamentally different from those in pure AF or pure d-wave phases, highlighting the unique interplay between coexisting AF and d-wave orders. Crucially, conventional s-wave superconductors cannot generate such mid-gap states in response to nonmagnetic impurities. This qualitative difference in impurity response provides a diagnostic tool to experimentally differentiate between the anisotropic s-wave and AF-d-wave coexistence scenarios. Scanning tunneling microscopy measurements of LDOS around nonmagnetic impurities could therefore resolve this fundamental question regarding the pairing mechanism in electron-doped cuprates, offering direct insight into the nature of superconductivity in these materials.

# Abstract

# Abstract

A quantitative method is presented for eliminating the intrinsic precession of a spherical pendulum caused by ellipsoidal motion. Removing this unwanted precession makes the Foucault precession due to Earth's rotation readily observable. The method is insensitive to both the magnitude and direction of perturbative forces inducing ellipsoidal motion. We demonstrate that even a short (three-meter) pendulum can be driven in a controlled manner to make Foucault precession dominant. This approach enables more accurate and practical construction of room-height or tabletop Foucault pendula, expanding accessibility to this classic demonstration of Earth's rotation.

# Abstract

We present results from a radial velocity survey of 179 red giant stars conducted at Lick Observatory since 1999, with approximately 20-100 measurements per star at 5-8 ms⁻¹ precision. We find that 80% (145 stars) exhibit radial velocity variations exceeding 20 ms⁻¹, with 43 showing significant periodicities. To determine the physical origin of these variations, we employ two complementary approaches: examining correlations between velocity amplitude and stellar surface gravity, and analyzing spectral line profile variations compared with theoretical models. These investigations aim to distinguish between planetary companions and intrinsic stellar phenomena such as oscillations or rotational modulation as sources of the observed radial velocity variations in evolved stars.

# Abstract

We present an analysis of gamma-ray observations from the Fermi Large Area Telescope toward the supernova remnant (SNR) Monoceros Loop (G205.5+0.5). Our spatial analysis reveals that the brightest gamma-ray emission is associated with the Rosette Nebula, a molecular cloud complex located adjacent to the southeastern boundary of the SNR. After modeling and subtracting this component, we identify extended gamma-ray emission from the SNR itself, which is well-described by a Gaussian spatial template. Spectral analysis demonstrates that both regions are better fit by curved spectral models than simple power-law functions. The gamma-ray luminosities in the 0.2-300 GeV energy range are measured to be ~10^34 erg s^-1 for the SNR and ~10^35 erg s^-1 for the Rosette Nebula. We interpret this emission as originating from interactions between particles accelerated by the SNR shock and ambient material. The spectral and spatial characteristics are consistent with hadronic processes, specifically the production and subsequent decay of neutral pions generated through collisions between accelerated protons and interstellar gas nuclei. This scenario provides a coherent explanation for the observed gamma-ray emission from both the Monoceros Loop SNR and the Rosette Nebula complex.

# Abstract

We investigate energy losses from astrophysical plasmas into Kaluza-Klein modes, extending previous work by Barger et al. that employed a zero-density approximation. Our analysis incorporates finite-density effects for two-plasmon processes, revealing distinctive behavior in the energy loss rate. For fixed temperature, we demonstrate that the energy loss rate per unit volume remains approximately constant below a critical density threshold, after which it decreases exponentially. This characteristic behavior is consistently observed for both transverse and longitudinal plasmons across direct and crossed channels, spanning a broad range of temperatures and densities. We address technical challenges associated with formulating the appropriate covariant interaction energy in finite-density, finite-temperature environments. Our findings validate the zero-density approximation employed by Barger et al., confirming that neglecting other plasmon processes introduces errors of less than one order of magnitude for their considered parameter regimes. These results have important implications for astrophysical constraints on extra-dimensional theories.

# Abstract

We investigate transport properties and circulating currents in Sierpinski gasket (SPG) fractals under applied bias voltage through side-attached electrodes. Exploiting the self-similar nature of SPG structures, we systematically examine loop currents and magnetic field distributions across multiple fractal generations. Our analysis reveals that physical quantities exhibit characteristic regularities when progressing through successive generations for fixed electrode configurations. A particularly significant finding is that introducing anisotropy in the hopping parameters leads to enhanced overall transport current magnitude. We present detailed calculations of the total conductance and individual loop currents, demonstrating how the fractal geometry influences quantum transport. These results provide insights into the interplay between self-similarity, quantum interference, and directional hopping asymmetry in fractal networks, with potential applications in understanding transport phenomena in complex nanostructures and fractal-based quantum devices.

While all gas with column densities @xmath5@xmath6 pc@xmath7 exhibits ongoing star formation, the fraction of star-forming gas declines with decreasing column density, reaching approximately 50% at @xmath8@xmath6 pc@xmath7. Remarkably, even in the densest gas regions, star formation efficiency is at least @xmath9 times lower than typical values observed in spiral galaxy star-forming regions. This trend is unlikely attributable to dust extinction, as the implied dust-to-gas ratios would be unrealistically high. Instead, we propose that this correlation reflects preferential formation of massive (@xmath10-producing) stars in high-density gas regions.
