# Abstract

Chemically peculiar A (Ap) stars represent extreme manifestations of atomic diffusion processes operating in the presence of strong magnetic fields within stellar atmospheres. The rapidly oscillating Ap (roAp) stars offer unique opportunities to probe these processes three-dimensionally while simultaneously constraining pulsation excitation mechanisms in A-type stars. We present results from an ongoing systematic, high-resolution spectroscopic survey of southern hemisphere Ap stars, utilizing the Michigan Spectral Catalogues for target selection. We report the discovery of seventeen new magnetic Ap stars exhibiting spectroscopically resolved Zeeman splitting, from which we derive magnetic field moduli ranging from @xmath0 kG. Notable discoveries include: (1) the second-strongest magnetic field currently known among A-type stars, (2) a double-lined spectroscopic binary system containing a magnetic Ap component, and (3) an A star displaying exceptionally peculiar and time-variable elemental abundances. Follow-up polarimetric observations of these objects are required to characterize their magnetic field geometries and determine rotational periods. Additionally, we present a new magnetic field measurement for the previously known Ap star HD 92499. These discoveries expand our understanding of extreme magnetic fields in intermediate-mass stars and provide new targets for detailed asteroseismic and magnetic field topology studies.

We extend the invaded cluster (IC) dynamics of Machta et al. to the fully frustrated Ising model on a square lattice. This dynamics exhibits numerical evidence of self-organized criticality. We demonstrate that fluctuations in the IC dynamics are intrinsic to the algorithm, causing the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to break down. The relaxation time is remarkably short and shows no critical size dependence, distinguishing this approach from conventional dynamics. These results highlight the unique non-equilibrium properties of IC dynamics when applied to frustrated systems, providing insights into self-organized critical behavior in geometrically frustrated magnets.

# Abstract

We investigate heat conduction in the spin-@xmath0 @xmath1 chain subjected to finite magnetic fields, where magnetothermal effects become significant. The model's integrability leads to divergent transport coefficients, manifested through finite Drude weights. Employing exact diagonalization and mean-field theory, we examine how the thermal Drude weight varies with temperature and magnetic field across different exchange anisotropies, maintaining zero magnetization-current flow conditions. Our analysis reveals three key findings: First, the Drude weight exhibits pronounced magnetic field dependence, with its magnitude decreasing under stronger fields and displaying non-monotonic behavior in peak position. Second, for weak exchange anisotropies and magnetic fields in both the massless and fully polarized regimes, mean-field predictions show excellent agreement with exact diagonalization results. Third, at the field-induced quantum critical line separating the paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases, we identify and propose a universal low-temperature scaling behavior of the thermal Drude weight, providing insights into the transport properties near quantum criticality in integrable spin systems.

# Abstract

Sequential measurements of non-commuting quantum observables yield joint probability distributions that fundamentally differ from classical statistics. We experimentally demonstrate that such measurements can be consistently described by a complex-valued quasi-probability distribution, where imaginary correlations between resolution errors and measurement back-action play a crucial role. Using weak-to-strong measurements of photon polarization, we implement a tunable-strength measurement scheme that precisely controls the correlation structure between sequential observations of diagonal and horizontal/vertical polarizations. Our experimental results reveal that the complex joint probability distribution characterizing an elliptically polarized input state remains invariant across different measurement strengths, with the imaginary component quantifying the intrinsically quantum correlations between measurement errors. This invariance provides direct evidence for the fundamental role of complex probability amplitudes in quantum mechanics and establishes a practical framework for quantum state tomography using sequential measurements. The imaginary error correlations we observe cannot be explained by any classical statistical model, highlighting the irreducible non-classical nature of quantum measurement processes and offering new insights into quantum information processing protocols.

# Abstract

We present high-dispersion spectroscopic observations of two superflare stars, KIC 9766237 and KIC 9944137, obtained with Subaru/HDS. Superflare stars are solar-type (G-type) main-sequence stars that exhibit flares orders of magnitude more energetic than typical solar flares, discovered through Kepler photometry. While most superflare stars show rotation periods shorter than 10 days, our targets have significantly longer periods of 21.8 and 25.3 days, making them particularly interesting for solar comparison.

Our spectroscopic analysis reveals that both stars possess fundamental parameters—effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity—remarkably similar to the Sun. The measured projected rotational velocities (v sin i) are consistent with the photometric rotation periods, suggesting high inclination angles. Using the Ca II 8542 Å absorption line as a diagnostic, we estimate average surface magnetic field strengths of 1–20 G for these stars.

We find no spectroscopic evidence for binary companions in our data, though additional observations are required to definitively exclude the presence of low-mass companions. The close similarity between these slowly rotating superflare stars and the Sun in terms of spectroscopic properties, rotation rates, and magnetic field characteristics strengthens the possibility that the Sun itself may be capable of producing superflares. These results have important implications for understanding extreme space weather events and assessing the potential for catastrophic solar activity that could impact Earth's technological infrastructure.

# Abstract

We apply chiral perturbation theory to investigate Lorentz violation in the strong-interaction sector of the Standard-Model Extension, focusing on the CPT-even pure-gluon operator in the minimal framework. We construct the lowest-order chiral effective Lagrangian for both two and three light quark flavors and establish consistent power-counting rules. Using heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory, we compute Lorentz-violating contributions to the nucleon self-energy and derive the first stringent experimental constraints on multiple components of the relevant Lorentz-violating coupling parameter. Our analysis yields bounds that significantly restrict the parameter space for Lorentz violation in QCD. Additionally, we obtain the Lorentz-violating nucleon-nucleon potential, which provides a theoretical foundation for extracting improved limits from high-precision experiments. We propose that atomic-clock comparisons and deuteron storage-ring measurements offer promising avenues for tightening these constraints, potentially improving sensitivity to Lorentz violation in hadronic systems by several orders of magnitude.

# Abstract

Unbounded outflows in the form of highly collimated jets and broad winds appear to be a ubiquitous feature of accreting black hole systems. The most powerful jets are thought to derive a significant fraction, if not the majority, of their power from the rotational energy of the black hole. Whatever the precise mechanism that causes them, these jets must therefore exert a braking torque on the black hole. Consequently, we expect jet production to play a significant role in limiting the maximum spin attainable by accreting black holes through accretion processes.

In this work, we calculate the spin-up function—defined as the rate of change of black hole spin normalized to the black hole mass and accretion rate—for an accreting black hole, explicitly accounting for this braking torque. We assume that the accretion flow onto a Kerr black hole is advection-dominated (ADAF) and construct easy-to-use analytic fits to describe the global structure of such flows based on the numerical solutions of Popham & Gammie (1998). 

We find that the predicted black hole spin-up function depends only on the black hole spin and dimensionless parameters describing the accretion flow properties. Using recent relativistic magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) numerical simulation results to calibrate the efficiency of angular momentum transfer in the flow, we find that an ADAF flow alone will spin a black hole up (or down) to an equilibrium value of approximately 0.95-0.98 of the maximal spin value in the absence of jets.

Combining our ADAF system with a simple model for jet power extraction, we demonstrate that when jet production is included, an equilibrium is reached at approximately 0.9 of the maximal spin value, consistent with recent numerical simulation studies of the spin-up of accreting black holes. At this equilibrium point, the spin-up of the hole by accreted material is precisely balanced by the braking torque arising from jet production.

The existence of this equilibrium spin has important implications. First, it means that optically-dim active galactic nuclei (AGN) that have grown via accretion from an advection-dominated flow will not be maximally rotating, but will instead settle at a predictable sub-maximal spin value. Second, it offers a possible explanation for the tight correlation observed between the Bondi accretion rate and jet power in nine nearby, X-ray luminous giant elliptical galaxies. We suggest that the black holes in these galaxies must all be rotating close to their equilibrium value, which naturally produces the observed tight correlation.

Our model also yields a relationship between jet efficiency and black hole spin that is in surprisingly good agreement with that seen in detailed simulation studies, indicating that our simple model provides a useful and convenient description of the coupled ADAF inflow-jet outflow system about a spinning black hole. This formulation is particularly suitable for incorporation in semi-analytic modeling as well as cosmological numerical simulation studies focusing on the formation and evolution of galaxies, groups, and clusters of galaxies.

# Abstract

We investigate the nonlocal Davey-Stewartson I equation through the Darboux transformation method, deriving explicit solution expressions. While nonlocal equations in higher dimensions typically exhibit singularities similar to their 1+1 dimensional counterparts, we demonstrate that singularity-free solutions can be constructed through careful parameter selection in the Lax pair. We rigorously prove that solutions generated via degree-@xmath1 Darboux transformations from two specific seed solutions—the trivial zero solution and an exponential function of @xmath0—yield global, non-singular solutions to the nonlocal Davey-Stewartson I equation. When constructed from the zero seed, these solutions constitute genuine soliton solutions characterized by boundedness and @xmath1 distinct peaks. Alternatively, employing the exponential seed solution produces "line dark soliton" solutions, which remain bounded while exhibiting rapid norm variations along specific linear trajectories. These results provide explicit families of physically meaningful, singularity-free solutions for this nonlocal integrable system.

# Abstract

We present a stochastic model for social networks that accounts for dynamic membership, where new actors may join, existing actors may become inactive, and previously inactive actors may reactivate. The model captures network evolution through a preferential attachment mechanism, whereby actors establish new connections or become active with probabilities proportional to their current connectivity or activity levels. We derive the mean-field equations governing the system's behavior and prove that the asymptotic distribution of actor connections follows a power-law. This framework is particularly applicable to various social network contexts, including wireless local area networks (WLANs), where users connect to access points, and peer-to-peer networks with direct user-to-user connections. To validate our theoretical predictions, we analyze empirical data from a publicly available dataset containing three years of wireless network traces from Dartmouth College. The analysis demonstrates strong agreement between our model and observed behavior, confirming that user access patterns asymptotically converge to a power-law distribution. Our results provide both theoretical insights into dynamic network formation and practical validation through real-world network data, establishing the model's utility for understanding temporal dynamics in evolving social networks.

# Abstract

The ubiquitous nature of modern information retrieval and virtual environments gives rise to novel conceptual realities whose ontological status and appropriate mathematical descriptions remain uncertain. This essay examines three paradigmatic examples illustrating this phenomenon. First, adaptive neural networks that, despite their nomenclature, are neither networks nor neural in traditional senses, yet provide services extending classical artificial neural network functionality. Second, the emergence of structures resembling Einsteinian spacetime that model internet user behavior as geodesic motion through information manifolds. Third, the demonstration and application of nonclassical probability structures in information retrieval, including probability distributions exhibiting stronger-than-quantum characteristics. These immense, operable datasets constitute new operationalistic environments that increasingly function as autonomous "realities." Following Melucci's metaphor, the information retrieval process is conceptualized as an objective physical process amenable to experimental investigation. Various semantic environments are treated as analogs of distinct physical realities. The essay advocates for the topos-theoretic approach to physical theories as providing a natural conceptual and technical framework for addressing these emerging realities, offering mathematical structures capable of accommodating the non-classical features inherent in information-theoretic phenomena.

Notably, we find significant discrepancies with constituent quark model predictions for several vector polarizabilities. # Abstract

We present a complete geometrical framework for effective Hamiltonians in nuclear shell model calculations. The theory is reformulated in manifestly geometric form, enabling reinterpretation and clarification of several aspects, including previously unknown or unpublished results. We provide detailed analysis of commuting observables and symmetries, accompanied by simple, explicit proofs. Novel numerical algorithms are proposed that enhance stability and improve upon current computational methods in shell model applications.

# Abstract

We report the detection of time-variable O line emission in a deep 100 ks Suzaku X-ray Imaging Spectrometer spectrum of the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission. The observed line intensity (11±2 line units or photons cm⁻² s⁻¹ str⁻¹) is anomalously strong for emission originating within the heavily obscured Galactic disk. The line exhibits a factor of two temporal variation that correlates significantly (>3σ) with the solar wind O⁶⁺ ion flux. This high intensity and strong temporal correlation with solar wind parameters strongly suggest a geocoronal solar wind charge exchange (SWCX) origin. We analyze the line intensity in the context of the observation geometry and theoretical models describing the spatial distribution of neutral hydrogen and solar wind ions around Earth. Our results demonstrate that X-ray observations of geocoronal SWCX emission provide a valuable diagnostic tool for constraining models of the near-Earth environment, including the exosphere and magnetosheath regions where charge exchange processes occur.

# Abstract

Data centre networks are critical infrastructure components that interconnect large numbers of servers to support cloud computing and related services. Traditional approaches, particularly fat-tree architectures, have dominated the design space, but recent work has explored alternative constructions based on combinatorial design theory. This paper investigates switch-centric data centre networks constructed via the @xmath0-step method, which utilizes carefully selected bipartite graphs and transversal designs to achieve high server counts with controlled network properties.

We provide a comprehensive theoretical analysis of path diversity in these combinatorially-constructed networks, establishing both the existence and optimality of various routing configurations. Our main contributions address two fundamental communication scenarios:

**One-to-one communication:** We prove the existence of maximal collections of pairwise link-disjoint paths connecting all servers adjacent to one switch with all servers adjacent to any other switch. These constructions are optimal in the number of disjoint paths achieved, and we demonstrate flexibility in the choice of underlying combinatorial structures (bipartite graphs and transversal designs) to which the @xmath0-step method can be applied. Critically, we maintain explicit control over path lengths, which directly impacts network latency.

**One-to-many communication:** We extend our analysis to broadcast-type scenarios, proving the existence of pairwise link-disjoint paths from all servers adjacent to a source switch to arbitrary identically-sized collections of target servers distributed throughout the network. Unlike the one-to-one case, target servers need not be co-located at a single switch, reflecting realistic communication patterns in distributed applications.

Our theoretical framework operates primarily on bipartite graphs, with applications to data centre networks following naturally from this abstraction. The results strengthen the case for combinatorially-designed data centre networks as viable alternatives to fat-tree architectures, demonstrating superior scalability while maintaining essential routing properties. More broadly, this work exemplifies the productive application of combinatorial mathematics to practical network design challenges, suggesting fertile ground for continued interdisciplinary research.

# Abstract

Long-term ("superorbital") periods or modulations have been detected in a wide variety of both low and high-mass X-ray binaries at X-ray and optical wavelengths. A variety of mechanisms have been proposed to account for the variability properties, such as precessing and/or warped accretion discs, amongst others. The All Sky Monitor on board the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer provides the most extensive (~15 years) and sensitive X-ray archive for studying such behaviour. It is also clear that such variations can be intermittent and/or a function of X-ray spectral state. Consequently, we use a time-dependent dynamic power spectrum method to examine how these modulations vary with time in 25 X-ray binaries for which superorbital periodicities have been previously reported. Our aim is to characterize these periodicities in a completely systematic way. We find that some systems (such as Her X-1 and LMC X-4) exhibit remarkably stable superorbital periods, while others show a range of properties, from even longer variability time-scales to quite chaotic behaviour. We discuss the implications of these results for the physical mechanisms responsible for superorbital modulations in X-ray binary systems.

# Abstract

This paper presents refined results on interpolation properties of planar spiral curves, extending previous work. The main contribution establishes boundary regions within which spiral and piecewise spiral splines can be constructed to match prescribed interpolation data. The width of these admissible regions provides a quantitative measure of the fairness and interpolability of given point sets. We demonstrate that this measure characterizes the geometric quality of data configurations and their suitability for smooth interpolation. Applications to tolerance control in manufacturing, particularly for curvilinear profile verification and quality assessment, are discussed and illustrated.

Active galactic nuclei (AGN) with relatively low-mass black holes provide crucial insights into black hole growth and evolution across cosmic time. We present comprehensive X-ray variability and spectral analysis of 15 newly identified candidates for AGN hosting low-mass black holes, selected from the Second XMM-Newton Serendipitous Source Catalogue based on their pronounced X-ray variability as quantified by normalized excess variance. 

Utilizing the established correlation between excess variance and black hole mass, we estimate masses ranging from @xmath0 @xmath1, with seven sources exhibiting masses below @xmath2 @xmath1—firmly in the intermediate-mass black hole regime. # Abstract

We investigate the temporal growth dynamics of the Internet by examining the relationship between node degree and growth rate fluctuations across multiple timescales. This transition manifests as Gibrat's law emerging in the small-degree region and progressively extending to larger degrees as the observation period increases. We quantify the validity regimes for both models and demonstrate that correlations between internal links significantly contribute to the emergence of Gibrat's law behavior. Our findings reveal that neither PA nor Gibrat's law fully captures Internet evolution dynamics independently, highlighting the need for a unified theoretical framework that incorporates both mechanisms to accurately model complex network growth in real-world systems.

# Abstract

# Abstract

We investigate bound-state broadening at unconventional superconductor interfaces induced by bulk impurity scattering using quasiclassical theory. Impurity effects are analyzed in both Born and unitarity limits. Our results demonstrate that unitary scatterers cause significantly weaker bound-state broadening compared to Born-limit scattering. We examine multiple model geometries and calculate the temperature-dependent Josephson critical current in the presence of impurity-broadened bound states. These findings reveal the crucial role of scattering mechanisms in determining interface properties and transport characteristics in unconventional superconducting junctions, with important implications for understanding quantum tunneling phenomena in strongly correlated superconducting systems.

# Abstract

We propose a scheme for on-demand generation of polarization-entangled N-photon states using trapped atoms in optical cavities. The protocol involves two key steps: first, preparing an entangled state of N atoms through postselective measurements on collective emission from multiple cavities coupled via a multiport beamsplitter; second, coherently mapping this atomic entanglement onto photonic degrees of freedom. This cavity-QED-based approach overcomes probabilistic limitations of spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources, enabling deterministic generation of multiphoton entangled states. Such controllable sources are crucial for scalable linear optics quantum computing, secure quantum cryptography, and precision tests of quantum nonlocality with increasing particle numbers.

# Abstract

We study the two-point correlator of a modified confined-Coulomb transition order parameter in four-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory with Wilson action. Its long-distance behavior in the confined phase is governed by single-particle decay. The mass of this particle is computed and found to be in agreement with previous calculations of the 0++ gaugeball mass. Remarkably, our order parameter allows extraction of good signal-to-noise ratios for masses with low statistics. The results provide a numerical check of theorems about the Hilbert space structure describing the confined phase of four-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theories. Our findings demonstrate the utility of this modified order parameter in efficiently probing the particle spectrum and validating theoretical predictions about confinement in compact gauge theories.

# Abstract

We examine two recently proposed models of charge ordering (CO) in nominally quarter-filled, quasi-one-dimensional organic charge transfer solids. These models are distinguished by their characteristic site charge density patterns: "1010" (alternating charges) and "1100" (charge pairing). Using the Peierls-extended Hubbard model, we incorporate both electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions to investigate the competition between these CO states.

First, we demonstrate that Hartree-Fock mean field theory yields qualitatively and quantitatively incorrect predictions for the critical nearest-neighbor Coulomb repulsion required to stabilize the "1010" ordered state, when compared with exact many-body calculations for the purely electronic Hamiltonian. Second, we establish that spin-Peierls order can emerge in both CO patterns and construct a comprehensive phase diagram incorporating on-site and inter-site electron-phonon coupling. Third, we analyze the expected temperature dependence of CO and metal-insulator transitions for both ordering patterns.

Finally, we compare our theoretical predictions with experimental observations, demonstrating that the "1100" CO state is clearly realized in 1:2 anionic charge transfer salts and (TMTSF)₂X materials. However, results for (TMTTF)₂X compounds with narrower bandwidths remain ambiguous, suggesting that the nearest-neighbor Coulomb interaction in these materials lies near the critical value separating the two CO regimes. Our findings provide a framework for understanding CO patterns across different families of quasi-one-dimensional organic conductors.

# Abstract

Finding satisfying assignments for variables involved in constraint satisfaction problems can be formulated as a bounded model generation problem: searching for bounded models of a theory in some logical framework. The current state-of-the-art approach for bounded model generation in rich knowledge representation languages (such as FO(·) and ASP) and constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) modeling languages (such as MiniZinc) is the ground-and-solve paradigm. This approach reduces the theory to a ground or propositional form and then applies a search algorithm to the resulting theory. However, a critical bottleneck in this method is the exponential blow-up in theory size caused by the grounding phase, which can render problems intractable.

Lazy grounding—deferring the grounding of theory components until necessary during search—offers a promising solution to this bottleneck. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and practical implementation for lazy grounding in the context of the FO(·) knowledge representation language. Our approach avoids grounding all parts of a theory by deriving justifications for selected components. Given a partial assignment for the grounded portion of the theory and valid justifications for formulas in the non-grounded portion, these justifications provide a constructive recipe for extending the partial assignment to a complete satisfying assignment.

During search, when a justification becomes invalid, we derive a new one; if this fails, we strategically split the formula into a part requiring grounding and a part that can be justified. Experimental results demonstrate that this lazy grounding approach significantly improves performance and showcases both the power and generality of our framework across diverse problem domains.

We present VLA 21-cm observations of the galaxy ESO 481-G017 to investigate the environment and formation mechanism of an isolated HII region located 43 kpc in projection from the galaxy center. The remote HII region exhibits an Hα luminosity of @xmath3 erg s@xmath4 with minimal continuum emission, suggesting recent star formation in a region with little or no pre-existing stellar population. The significant velocity offset between the HI disk of ESO 481-G017 (3840-4000 km s@xmath4) and the isolated HII region (4701±80 km s@xmath4) suggests two possible origins: star formation within a tidal feature or triggered star formation in a very low-luminosity companion galaxy. Our VLA observations provide crucial insights into the nature and formation history of this unusual star-forming region.

# Abstract

Our analysis reveals that the longest bursts (@xmath0 s) exhibit the most robust power-law PDSs, with self-similar time scales spanning more than two decades. We apply this PDS methodology as a sensitive diagnostic tool for GRB studies. Energy-dependent analysis of bright bursts reveals systematic spectral variations: the PDS flattens in hard energy channels (@xmath3 keV) and steepens in soft channels (@xmath4 keV), while bolometric light curves approximately follow the @xmath5 law. 

Comparing dim and bright bursts, we discover a strong correlation between burst brightness and PDS slope. This correlation indicates that GRBs are not standard candles, and dim bursts are intrinsically weak rather than merely distant. The observed time dilation in dim bursts likely originates from intrinsic physical processes within the burst itself rather than cosmological redshift effects. These findings have important implications for understanding GRB physics and the interpretation of burst populations.

# Abstract

# Abstract

We analyze collisional decoherence of atoms or molecules prepared in coherent superpositions of nondegenerate internal states at ultralow temperatures within an ultracold buffer gas. Our treatment is valid for arbitrary bath-to-tracer particle mass ratios. Both elastic and inelastic collisions contribute to decoherence processes. We derive an expression connecting the observable decoherence rate to fundamental pairwise scattering properties, particularly low-temperature scattering amplitudes. Special attention is given to the mass-ratio dependence in the regime of light bath particles and heavy tracer species. These analytical expressions provide accurate decoherence rate estimates essential for low-temperature applications. Our results suggest a novel experimental method: determining scattering lengths of atoms and molecules in different internal states through measurements of decoherence-induced damping of coherent oscillations. This approach offers a new spectroscopic tool for characterizing ultracold collision dynamics and extracting interaction potentials from observed decoherence timescales.

# Abstract

This paper presents a workshop designed for grade eleven high school students conducted during a university open day, introducing the abstract mathematical concept of metric spaces. The pedagogical approach employed a two-stage methodology: participants initially explored fundamental properties of distance through concrete, real-life examples to develop intuitive understanding. Following this preparatory phase, the formal definition of metric spaces was systematically introduced. Students then engaged with the abstract concepts through collaborative problem-oriented exercise sessions in small groups, allowing for active learning and peer discussion. This workshop demonstrates an effective bridge between intuitive geometric understanding and formal mathematical abstraction, making advanced mathematical concepts accessible to pre-university students while maintaining mathematical rigor and fostering collaborative problem-solving skills.

# Abstract

We report the discovery of a variable, compact steep spectrum radio source located ~65 arcsec (~4 kpc) from the center of the starburst galaxy NGC 3310, detected during an ongoing radio supernova monitoring program. At the distance of NGC 3310, the source exhibits a 5 GHz luminosity of approximately 10^26 W Hz^-1. The combination of its high luminosity, variability characteristics, compact structure (~17 mas), and spatial association with HII regions strongly suggests this is a previously uncatalogued Type II radio supernova. Analysis of archival data reveals an associated X-ray source with luminosity consistent with known radio supernovae. These multi-wavelength observations provide compelling evidence for ongoing massive star formation and supernova activity in NGC 3310's starburst environment, contributing to our understanding of supernova rates in starburst galaxies.

# Abstract

Motivated by the foundational work of McClure and Dyer (Class. Quantum Grav. **23**, 1971 (2006)), we present a comprehensive analysis of solutions to the Einstein-Maxwell equations that describe charged black holes embedded in cosmological backgrounds. Our investigation begins with a detailed examination of electromagnetic sources for a sufficiently general metric ansatz, systematically deriving the electromagnetic four-current and conserved electric charge for each configuration.

We revisit the charged McVittie solution, performing a thorough study of its causal structure. Our analysis demonstrates that this solution can represent a charged black hole in an expanding universe, with the notable feature that the black hole horizon forms only at infinite late times. We extend our investigation to charged versions of metrics originally proposed by Vaidya (VD) and Sultana-Dyer (SD), revealing that the charged Sultana-Dyer metric necessarily requires a global electric current in addition to a central spherically symmetric electric charge.

To facilitate comparison with the charged McVittie metric, we construct new generalized charged solutions of both VD and SD types, wherein the original mass and charge parameters are promoted to specific functions of cosmological time. Our analysis reveals distinct evolutionary behaviors: in the generalized charged Vaidya metric, the black hole horizon never forms, while in the generalized Sultana-Dyer case, both Cauchy and black hole horizons develop asymptotically at infinite late times.

We also introduce and analyze a charged version of the Thakurta metric, representing a novel solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations. Similar to the charged Sultana-Dyer case, the electromagnetic field in this spacetime is sourced by both a central electric charge and an additional global electric current. A study of the global causal structure confirms that this spacetime can indeed represent a charged black hole in a cosmological background.

A common feature of all solutions examined is the presence of initial singularities, analogous to those found in the original McVittie metric. Our work provides new insights into the interplay between electromagnetic fields, black hole horizons, and cosmological expansion, offering a systematic framework for understanding charged black holes in dynamical spacetimes.

# Abstract

We present a refined phase-connected post-glitch timing ephemeris for the Geminga pulsar that successfully fits all available post-glitch data from EGRET and subsequent observations. Phase-resolved spectroscopic analysis of two X-ray observations obtained in 2002 and 2004 is performed to investigate the pulsar's emission properties. We critically examine a previously reported detection of a small hot spot on the neutron star surface. Our analysis demonstrates that this claimed feature was likely an artifact resulting from overly restrictive modeling assumptions, specifically the constraint of a constant spectral index for the non-thermal emission component. When we permit the spectral index to vary with rotational phase, we observe systematic phase-dependent variations in this parameter. Importantly, these more flexible spectral models adequately describe the observations without requiring an additional hot blackbody component, thereby challenging the existence of the previously claimed hot spot feature.

# Abstract

We present a model explaining bipolar resistive switching in transition metal oxides through electric field-enhanced oxygen vacancy migration at the nanoscale. Our numerical analysis reveals that intense electric fields concentrate at highly resistive dielectric-electrode interfaces, producing spatially inhomogeneous oxygen vacancy distributions that drive the resistive switching phenomenon. The model successfully captures the underlying physical mechanisms governing the non-volatile resistance changes characteristic of these materials. We validate our theoretical framework against experimental resistance hysteresis measurements, demonstrating qualitative agreement with non-trivial switching behaviors. This combined theoretical-experimental approach provides fundamental insights into the interfacial processes controlling resistive switching in oxide-based memory devices.

# Abstract

Whole genome sequencing (WGS) has rapidly transitioned from an ambitious research endeavor to an accessible technology with transformative potential for personalized medicine and disease understanding. While WGS promises revolutionary healthcare applications through improved diagnosis, treatment selection, and disease prevention, it simultaneously introduces significant privacy and ethical concerns. Human genomic data uniquely identifies individuals and reveals sensitive information about disease susceptibility, ancestry, and familial relationships, creating unprecedented privacy risks. This article examines the tension between genomic innovation and privacy protection by reviewing recent technological advances in WGS and analyzing the resulting privacy implications. We identify critical research challenges including secure data storage and sharing, protection against re-identification attacks, informed consent in the genomic era, and balancing scientific progress with individual privacy rights, highlighting the urgent need for comprehensive privacy-preserving frameworks.

# Abstract

We extend Lynch's analysis of random Boolean networks as models for genetic regulatory networks beyond the original constraints. While Lynch proved Kauffman's conjecture regarding the abundance of ineffective and freezing gates in the ordered phase versus their scarcity in the disordered phase for networks with connectivity K=2 and non-uniform Boolean function probabilities, we generalize these results to networks with arbitrary connectivity K and biased Boolean functions. Our key contribution demonstrates that Lynch's parameter λ is equivalent to the expectation of average sensitivity of Boolean functions used in network construction, enabling application of established theorems on average sensitivity. For networks with biased functions, we derive the expectation of average sensitivity when randomly selecting functions with specific connectivity and bias parameters. This generalization provides a more comprehensive theoretical foundation for understanding phase transitions in random Boolean networks, confirming that the relationship between network dynamics and structural properties holds across broader parameter spaces. Our results strengthen the mathematical underpinnings of Boolean network models in computational biology and complex systems theory.

# Abstract

We present a comprehensive theoretical investigation of electron-positron pair creation in collisions between a laser beam and a nonlaser photon using the S-matrix formalism. The laser field is modeled as a finite pulse, extending our previously developed framework for Compton scattering. We examine the nonperturbative regime where the laser intensity is sufficiently high that perturbative approaches become inadequate. Our calculations focus on energy-angular distributions of the created particles under various field configurations.

A key finding is that energy spectra computed using the finite pulse model show excellent agreement with those obtained via the modulated plane wave approximation when the laser pulse duration is sufficiently long. However, significant deviations emerge for short pulses, highlighting the importance of proper pulse modeling. We demonstrate that pair production rates exhibit strong polarization dependence in the nonperturbative regime, with linear polarization yielding maximal production rates. Consequently, we conduct detailed analysis of how the relative orientation of linear polarizations between the laser pulse and nonlaser photon affects pair creation efficiency.

Furthermore, we explore carrier-envelope phase effects on angular distributions of created particles, revealing the potential for phase control in pair production processes. Our results provide important insights for experimental design and interpretation in strong-field quantum electrodynamics, particularly for next-generation high-intensity laser facilities approaching the nonperturbative regime.

# Abstract

We present the realization of a two-dimensional permanent magnetic lattice consisting of Ioffe-Pritchard microtraps for ultracold atoms. The lattice is created using a single 300 nm thick magnetized FePt layer, patterned via optical lithography. Our system features over 15,000 tightly confining microtraps with a remarkably high density of 1250 traps/mm². We develop simple analytical approximations to characterize the magnetic fields generated by the lattice structure and determine key trap parameters. Experimental demonstration shows successful loading of ultracold atoms into at least 30 lattice sites positioned approximately 10 μm above the film surface. This work represents a significant advancement toward implementing quantum information processing protocols using neutral atoms confined in magnetic lattice potentials, offering scalability and precise control for future quantum applications.

# Abstract

We perform numerical simulations of the lattice-animal problem at the upper critical dimension @xmath0 on hypercubic lattices to investigate logarithmic corrections to scaling. Our stochastic sampling method employs the pruned-enriched Rosenbluth method (PERM), adapted from linear polymer studies, achieving high statistics for animals with up to 8000 sites. We estimate partition sums (total number of distinct animals) and radii of gyration. Our results confirm the Parisi-Sourlas prediction for leading critical exponents and compare logarithmic-correction exponents against two competing theoretical predictions from literature. The data discriminate between these predictions. Additionally, we propose and verify a novel Parisi-Sourlas-type scaling relation specifically applicable to logarithmic-correction exponents, providing new theoretical insight into critical phenomena at the upper critical dimension for branched polymers.

# Abstract

We construct numerous exact solutions to the nonlinear mean-field Gross-Pitaevskii equations describing multicomponent Bose-Einstein condensates confined in one-, two-, and three-dimensional optical lattices. Both stationary and nonstationary solutions are presented in closed analytical form. Notable examples include a vortex-antivortex array configuration on square optical lattices and oscillatory modes where multiple components periodically transfer between adjacent potential wells. For condensates on simple cubic lattices, we obtain diverse solutions, including a particularly interesting configuration where one component remains stationary while the other exhibits flow through a complex three-dimensional network of intersecting vortex lines. Through direct numerical integration of the time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii equations, we demonstrate that several physically significant solutions maintain dynamical stability over extended parameter ranges, confirming their potential experimental relevance and observability in ultracold atomic systems.

We reexamine the classical problem of tippe top dynamics, specifically analyzing the spinning and inversion behavior of an eccentric sphere model on a horizontal table. Our analysis employs a modified Coulomb friction law that depends continuously on the slip velocity @xmath0 at the contact point and vanishes at @xmath1, providing a more physically realistic treatment than traditional discontinuous models.

A central focus of our investigation is the relevance of the gyroscopic balance condition (GBC) to the tippe top inversion phenomenon. This condition, originally discovered by Moffatt and Shimomura in their study of rapidly spinning hard-boiled eggs, plays a crucial but different role in tippe top dynamics. We introduce a diagnostic variable @xmath2 where @xmath3 indicates satisfaction of the GBC, and track its evolution throughout the motion.

Our key finding is that unlike the spinning egg case, the tippe top does not initially satisfy the GBC. However, numerical simulations reveal that tippe tops destined to invert do approximately satisfy the GBC shortly after the motion begins. This observation proves fundamental to understanding the inversion mechanism.

Through analysis combining the GBC with geometric constraints, we establish a complete classification of tippe tops into three distinct groups based on their inversion behavior: Group I tippe tops never invert regardless of initial spin; Group II exhibits complete inversion when spun sufficiently rapidly; and Group III inverts only to a maximum inclination angle @xmath4 where @xmath5 holds.

We identify three steady states for the spinning motion and develop a new stability criterion to analyze these states as functions of the initial spin velocity @xmath6. This analysis yields a critical initial spin value @xmath7 necessary for Group II tippe tops to achieve complete inversion. Our results provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding this fascinating dynamical system, resolving longstanding questions about the conditions governing tippe top inversion.

We present a comprehensive tight-binding approach for computing Zeeman splittings in semiconductor nanostructures. The methodology operates within the electron-hole framework and naturally extends to exciton calculations through incorporation of Coulomb interactions. This technique effectively captures quantum confinement effects and g-factor anisotropy arising from nanostructure geometry. We demonstrate the method's capabilities through numerical calculations on CdSe and CdTe nanostructures, illustrating how structural morphology influences the magnetic response. The framework provides a versatile tool for investigating magnetooptical properties in confined semiconductor systems with arbitrary shapes.

in this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of deep near-infrared (nir) imaging observations of the globular cluster m4, obtained using the hubble space telescope's wide field camera 3 (hst/wfc3). our high-precision nir photometry has produced an exceptionally detailed colour-magnitude diagram (cmd) that clearly traces the main sequence down to and beyond the theoretical hydrogen-burning limit, while also revealing the white dwarf sequence. this represents the deepest nir cmd ever constructed for a globular cluster.

to enhance the reliability of our stellar classification, we incorporated archival hst optical data for proper-motion cleaning of the cmd and to distinguish between white dwarfs (wds) and brown dwarf (bd) candidates. our observations achieve remarkable detection limits of @xmath0 mag and @xmath1 mag in the nir bands, and @xmath2 mag in the optical.

by comparing our observed cmds with state-of-the-art theoretical stellar models, we confirm that our nir photometry extends beyond the hydrogen-burning limit, while our optical-nir cmds reach approximately to this critical boundary. this depth differential creates a unique opportunity: nir sources fainter than the h-burning limit without optical counterparts become potential bd candidates, as the optical observations lack sufficient depth to detect these extremely faint objects.

we conducted a systematic visual inspection of nir sources fainter than the h-burning limit in @xmath3 that lacked measured optical counterparts. this investigation identified five sources without optical photometry. for four of these, we detected faint optical emission and estimated upper magnitude limits. based on these constraints and comparison with theoretical models, we classify one source as likely a white dwarf, one as ambiguous (either wd or bd), and two as consistent with brown dwarfs. the fifth source, showing no detectable optical counterpart, represents our strongest bd candidate.

in total, we identify four compelling brown dwarf candidates in m4, demonstrating the power of combining ultra-deep nir imaging with complementary optical data for studying the substellar population in globular clusters.
